Manufacturer specifications for how long a particular job may take. This way the same job is charged the same in every workshop, however fast the mechanic actually was. Depending on the manufacturer, 10 or 12 AW make one hour. Formula to remember: labour charge on the invoice = number of AW × price per AW.
How often must a car go for the main inspection (HU)?
New cars for the first time after 36 months, then every 24 months. The emissions test is part of the HU.
What is a cost estimate?

An estimate of the repair costs. A non-binding estimate may only be exceeded significantly (guide value about 15 to 20 %) if the customer is informed beforehand. A binding estimate counts as a fixed price.
Explain the contractor's lien.
The workshop may keep the repaired vehicle until the invoice has been paid (§ 647 BGB).
Distinguish between registration certificate part I and part II.
Part I (formerly vehicle registration document): carry it with the vehicle. Part II (formerly vehicle title): keep it safe, important when selling, names the keeper, not necessarily the owner.
What is the CoC document?
The EU Certificate of Conformity. It confirms that the vehicle matches an approved type and is needed for first registration.
How is a workshop invoice structured?
Labour (AW × price per AW or hours × hourly rate) + parts and material − discount = net amount + 19 % VAT = invoice amount. Plus mandatory details such as date of service and tax number.
Which systems are distinguished in a vehicle?

Mechanical (e.g. cable of the parking brake), hydraulic (brakes, power steering on older vehicles), pneumatic (air brakes on trucks, air suspension), electrical and electronic (lighting, control units, ABS, ESP, electromechanical steering).
What do ABS and ESP do?
ABS stops the wheels from locking when braking, so the car can still be steered. ESP brakes individual wheels in a targeted way and so prevents skidding.
What is part of a visual inspection for road safety?
Lighting, tyres (tread legally at least 1,6 mm, damage, pressure), wipers and windows, fluid levels (brake fluid, coolant, oil), brakes, mirrors, first aid kit and warning triangle.
Why is brake fluid changed regularly?
It is hygroscopic, meaning it absorbs water. This lowers the boiling point and vapour bubbles can form, so the brakes fade. Usually changed every 2 years.
What is the CAN bus?
A data network in the vehicle through which the control units communicate. Faults are stored in the fault memory and read out with the diagnostic tester.
Distinguish between statutory warranty, a guarantee and goodwill.

Statutory warranty (liability for defects): by law, 2 years, against the seller. For used goods sold to consumers it can be shortened to 1 year if agreed expressly and separately. Guarantee: voluntary promise, usually by the manufacturer, conditions according to the guarantee certificate. Goodwill: voluntary gesture without legal entitlement, for customer loyalty.
What applies to data protection in customer service?

Use customer data only for the agreed purpose (e.g. order, invoice). Advertising by e-mail, phone or text message generally requires consent (exception: existing customers under § 7 (3) UWG). The customer can object to any advertising. Store data securely, do not pass it to unauthorised persons, delete it after the retention periods (GDPR).
How are end-of-life vehicles disposed of?
Only via an approved dismantling company or collection point. The keeper receives a certificate of destruction, which is needed for deregistration. Manufacturers must take back their vehicles.
What applies to used batteries and used oil?

Starter batteries: take-back obligation, 7,50 € deposit if no old battery is returned. Used oil: whoever sells engine oil must offer a collection point for the same amount of used oil. Store separately and leak-proof.
How does a dealership measure service quality?
Customer satisfaction surveys (e.g. a call after the workshop visit), complaint management, keeping to deadlines and cost ranges, repeat repairs, manufacturer standards.
What is an ABC analysis in the parts store?

Classifying items by their share of consumption value: A items = few items with a high value share (plan precisely, keep stock tight), C items = many items with a low value share (simplified planning), B items in between.
Which stocktaking methods are there?

Year-end stocktaking (physical count on the balance sheet date), shifted-date inventory (up to 3 months before or 2 months after the date, value rolled forward or back), perpetual inventory (continuous stock records, each item counted once a year), sample-based inventory (statistical methods).
Explain what average stock, average storage period and storage interest rate tell you.

Average stock shows the capital tied up in the warehouse. Using the 12 month-end stocks it is more precise than using only opening and closing stock. The storage period says how many days goods stay in stock on average. The storage interest rate shows how much interest the tied-up capital costs during this time: the shorter the storage period, the lower it is. Formula to remember: average stock = (opening stock + 12 month-end stocks) ÷ 13, simplified (opening + closing) ÷ 2; storage period = 360 ÷ turnover rate; storage interest rate = annual interest rate × storage period ÷ 360.
What does „delivered“ (Frei Haus) mean compared with „ex works“ (Ab Werk)?

Delivered (Frei Haus): the seller bears the transport costs up to the buyer. Between merchants, without a special agreement, the risk passes on handover to the carrier. Ex works (Ab Werk): from the seller's warehouse, the buyer bears costs and risk.
Which defect rights does the buyer have, and in what order?
First subsequent performance (repair or replacement). Only if this fails or is refused do withdrawal, price reduction and damages come into play.
Name methods of handling objections.

Yes-but method (agree, then counter-argument), boomerang method (objection becomes a buying argument), counter-question method (ask for the reason), pre-emption method (raise the expected objection yourself), reference method (satisfied customers as proof). Never dismiss objections.
What HU interval applies to taxis and other vehicles used for commercial passenger transport?
Every year, i.e. 12 months.
Which items does the EU tyre label show?

Fuel efficiency (rolling resistance), wet grip and external rolling noise (decibels and class A to C). Since 2021, where applicable, also symbols for snow and ice grip and a QR code for the EU product database.
How do you mention the price skilfully?

State the price only once the benefit is clear. Sandwich method: embed the price between two benefit arguments. Break the price into small units (e.g. per month or per 1,000 km). State the price confidently and without apologising.
What is the legal minimum tread depth for passenger cars?
1.6 mm, measured in the main groove.
What does the Blue Angel label mean?
An environmental label for products with a lower environmental impact, for paper for example made from waste paper.
How are room and heating costs allocated to departments?

Room and heating costs depend on how much floor area a department uses. So they are allocated by square metres: the more area, the more costs. Electricity is allocated more precisely by meter readings if there are separate meters. Formula to remember: total costs / total area × area of the department.
Distinguish between gross margin and mark-up.

Both describe the same amount between landed cost and selling price, but with a different base. The mark-up refers to the landed cost (purchasing view: how much do I add?). The margin refers to the selling price (sales view: how much of the price do I keep?). That is why the mark-up is always higher than the margin: a 25 % mark-up equals a 20 % margin. Formula to remember: mark-up = margin × 100 / (100 − margin); margin = mark-up × 100 / (100 + mark-up).
Explain which type of calculation applies at which step in backward calculation.

Customer discount and cash discount: deduct as a percentage of the price (× 0.9 etc.). Profit and overheads: work back by dividing by (1 + rate). Delivery costs: subtract. Supplier cash discount and discount: divide by (1 − rate).
Describe the structure of the cost-plus calculation for a workshop job.

Productive wages (hours × wage rate) + workshop overhead mark-up (rate from the cost allocation sheet, based on productive wages) = total cost + profit mark-up = net price for the labour. Parts are usually charged separately at their selling price.
Distinguish between pre-calculation and post-calculation and state their purpose.

Pre-calculation: before the job, using planned values (standard costs), to set the quoted price or cost estimate. Post-calculation: after the job, using actual values (actual costs), to identify variances and the actual result.
Explain mixed (compensatory) pricing.

Some products are sold at a low margin because of competition (e.g. new cars, special offers). Others with a higher margin (e.g. accessories, parts, service) make up for it. What matters is that the overall range covers all costs and makes a profit.
Describe what applies to declining-balance depreciation for acquisitions from July 2025.

For movable fixed assets acquired from July 2025 to December 2027: a fixed percentage of the remaining book value, at most three times the straight-line rate and no more than 30%. Pro rata by month in the first year. Switching to straight-line is allowed; switching back is not.
Explain the collective item (pool depreciation).

An optional alternative to the low-value asset rule: fixed assets from €250.01 to €1,000 net are grouped into one pool per year and depreciated at 20% a year over 5 years, even if an asset leaves earlier. The choice applies uniformly to all assets of this size in the financial year.
Describe how the sale of a fixed asset at a gain or loss is recorded.

The net selling price is compared with the remaining book value. If it is higher, there is a gain on disposal; if lower, a loss. The remaining book value is derecognised, and VAT is charged on the selling price.
Distinguish between accounting and imputed depreciation.

Accounting: based on acquisition cost, under commercial and tax law, over the standard useful life from the depreciation table; recorded in the P&L. Imputed: based on replacement value, over the actual useful life, continuing after the book value reaches zero; used in cost accounting and pricing.
Explain workshop utilisation, efficiency and productivity.

The three ratios show where time is lost in the workshop. Utilisation shows how much of the attendance time was spent on customer jobs (the rest is idle time, tidying up, training). Efficiency shows how fast the work was done: more sold than clocked hours means faster than the standard time. Productivity combines both: how much of the paid attendance could be sold? Formula to remember: utilisation = clocked / attendance hours; efficiency = sold / clocked hours; productivity = sold / attendance hours = utilisation × efficiency; each × 100.
Describe how to determine the hourly labour rate from workshop costs.

The rate must cover all workshop costs, spread over the hours that can really be sold to customers. So you divide all workshop costs (productive and unproductive wages, overheads, allocations from the cost allocation sheet) by the saleable hours and add the profit mark-up. Formula to remember: saleable hours = attendance hours × utilisation × efficiency.
Describe the steps of workshop job control.

Appointment and capacity planning, vehicle check-in with the customer, signed repair order (with cost estimate if needed), job allocation to mechanics, execution with time recording, customer approval for extra work, quality check, invoice, vehicle handover with explanation, follow-up.
Name the conditions under which a dealership may deduct input VAT.

The supply was received for the business, there is a proper invoice showing VAT separately, and the supply has been made. No deduction where the purchase is used for VAT-exempt sales (e.g. insurance brokerage) or where no VAT is shown, e.g. when buying a used car from a private seller.
Name the mandatory details of an invoice.

Name and address of supplier and recipient, tax number or VAT ID, issue date, sequential invoice number, quantity and type of supply, date of supply, net amount by tax rate, tax rate and tax amount (or a note on the exemption). Small invoices up to €250 gross need fewer details.
Describe what applies to e-invoicing between businesses (B2B).

Since 2025 all businesses must be able to receive e-invoices. Businesses with prior-year turnover above €800,000 must issue them from 2027, all businesses from 2028. An e-invoice is a structured format (e.g. XRechnung, ZUGFeRD); a plain PDF does not count. Small invoices up to €250 are exempt.
Explain when the new and used car sales conditions (NWVB/GWVB) apply to a purchase contract.

They are standard terms and conditions (a non-binding recommendation by the trade associations). They apply only if properly incorporated: express reference when the contract is concluded, a reasonable opportunity to read them and the customer's consent (§ 305(2) BGB). Individual agreements take precedence (§ 305b BGB).
Describe how a used car purchase contract is concluded under the GWVB.

The buyer's order is the offer; the buyer is bound by it for at most 10 days (commercial vehicles 2 weeks). The contract is formed when the seller confirms acceptance in text form within this period or delivers the vehicle.
Describe the buyer's rights if delivery of the new car is delayed.

With a non-binding date, the buyer can demand delivery no earlier than six weeks after it has passed, which puts the seller in default (with a binding date, immediately). The buyer can then set a reasonable additional period and withdraw from the contract once it has expired without result (§ 323 BGB); if the seller is at fault, damages can also be claimed.
Describe what applies if the buyer does not take delivery of the ordered vehicle.

The buyer must take delivery within the agreed period after receiving the notice of readiness. If not, the seller can withdraw after an unsuccessful deadline and claim damages. The sales conditions provide a lump-sum percentage of the purchase price for this; the buyer may prove that the loss was lower (§ 309 No. 5 BGB).
Assess whether the buyer may transfer rights under the new car purchase contract to a third party.
Under the NWVB only with the seller's prior consent. This allows the dealer to prevent ordered vehicles from being passed on to resellers, for example.
Explain when there is a material defect under § 434 BGB.

When, at the passing of risk, the item does not meet the subjective requirements (agreed quality, use assumed under the contract), the objective requirements (suitability for ordinary use, customary quality) or the assembly requirements. With consumers, a negative deviation is valid only if they were specifically informed and it was agreed expressly and separately (§ 476(1) BGB).
Distinguish between a complaint and an exchange.

Complaint: the goods are defective and the customer has statutory warranty rights (subsequent performance first). Exchange: the goods are free of defects, there is no legal right; an exchange is a goodwill gesture. Exception: 14-day right of withdrawal for distance and off-premises contracts.
When is a customer in default of payment and what follows?

Default after a reminder, without a reminder if a calendar date was fixed, at the latest 30 days after due date and receipt of the invoice (consumers only if the invoice says so). Consequences: default interest (consumers 5, businesses 9 percentage points above the base rate), compensation for damage caused by the delay, and a flat €40 fee towards businesses.
Name special warranty rules for consumer sales.

Limitation period generally 2 years from handover. For used goods (e.g. used cars) it can be shortened to 1 year, but only by an express, separate agreement. Reversed burden of proof: if a defect appears within one year, it is presumed to have existed at handover.
How does the workshop handle waste correctly?

Order of priority: avoid, reuse, recycle, otherwise recover, dispose. Collect waste separately (used oil, oil filters, brake fluid, coolant, batteries, oily rags) and do not mix it. Hand over hazardous waste only to licensed disposal companies with documentation; the business remains responsible as the waste producer.
What applies to refrigerant from the air-conditioning system?

Refrigerant must not be released into the environment. Extraction, recycling and refilling only with a suitable A/C service unit and only by staff with a certificate of competence. Old refrigerant is collected and disposed of properly.
Explain what church tax in the payslip is calculated on.
On the wage tax, not on the gross salary. In Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg it is 8 %, in the other states 9 % of the wage tax.
Assess whether a tax allowance also reduces social security contributions.

No. The allowance only reduces taxable pay and therefore the tax. Social security is calculated on the gross salary subject to social security, i.e. salary plus, for example, the employer contribution to capital-forming benefits.
Explain who pays the childless surcharge for long-term care insurance.
The employee alone. Childless employees aged 23 and over pay 0,6 % more, so their share rises from 1,8 % to 2,4 %. The employer share stays at 1,8 %.
Describe how to get from gross salary to net pay.

First work out the gross subject to social security. From it you deduct the taxes (wage tax, solidarity surcharge, church tax), which depend on taxable pay, and the employee shares of health, care, pension and unemployment insurance, which are calculated on the SV gross. Scheme to remember: SV gross − taxes − social security = net pay.
Assess a liquidity level 2 of 60 % at a dealership.

Without sales, the dealership can only pay 60 % of its short-term debts from cash and receivables; the 100 % rule of thumb is not reached. At a dealership this is not immediately dangerous, because vehicles can quickly be turned into cash as long as days in stock are short. Measures: reduce days in stock, collect receivables faster, refinance short-term loans.
Name measures a dealership can take to raise its equity ratio.

Do not distribute profits but retain them in the business. Partner contributions or new partners. Reduce debt, e.g. through smaller vehicle stocks and shorter days in stock. Sell assets that are not needed and repay debts.
Explain how to assess a ratio in the exam.

First state the value, then compare it with a benchmark: previous year (time comparison), other dealerships or the industry (company and industry comparison) or a rule of thumb. Then describe the consequence for the dealership and suggest a suitable measure.
Return on equity rises while return on sales falls. Explain how this fits together.

Return on sales relates profit to revenue, return on equity relates it to equity. If revenue rises sharply and profit only a little, return on sales falls. If at the same time equity has fallen, for example through withdrawals, or profit has risen slightly, return on equity still rises.
Name advantages and disadvantages of a lot of debt for a dealership.

Advantages: larger vehicle stocks and investments possible, positive leverage as long as return on total capital is above the interest rate, interest reduces taxable profit. Disadvantages: interest and repayment burden, dependence on banks and the manufacturer's bank, risk if interest rises or sales fall, poorer creditworthiness.
Distinguish between the target and the actual workshop index.

The target index is planned: target labour revenue (cost plus profit and risk, both calculated on cost) divided by productive wages. The actual index is what was really achieved: actual labour revenue divided by productive wages. If the actual index is below the target index, the workshop earned less than planned, for example through discounts, unbilled working time or hourly rates that are too low. It then does not fully cover its costs and the planned profit.
Explain how overheads are distributed to the cost centres in the BAB.

Costs that can be assigned directly are distributed per receipts, e.g. salaries per payroll or depreciation per asset register. The remaining costs are split with an allocation key that reflects causation as well as possible, e.g. rent by floor area or energy by share of consumption. Then the totals are formed, the service cost centre administration is allocated to the main cost centres (e.g. in the ratio of sales revenue), and the overhead rate is calculated for each main cost centre: overheads ÷ allocation base × 100.
quiz: 16-year-old Lena buys headphones for 45,00 € in an electronics store without her parents knowing and pays cash from her pocket money. Determine the legal position.
The contract is void because Lena, as a minor, lacks legal capacity.
The contract is provisionally ineffective until the parents expressly approve it.
The contract is valid from the start because Lena pays with funds given to her for free use.
The contract is valid, but the parents may withdraw from it within 14 days.
The contract is only valid because the price is below the statutory pocket-money limit of 50,00 €.
§ 110 BGB (pocket-money rule): the contract is valid if the person with limited capacity pays in full at once with funds given for free use. There is no fixed amount limit.

A customer of Autohaus Nordring GmbH buys a set of winter wheels and pays at once at the till. He agrees to collect the wheels in three days; nothing else is agreed. Determine who holds ownership and possession until collection.
The customer became owner and possessor on payment.
The customer is owner, the dealership is possessor of the wheels.
The dealership is owner, the customer is already possessor of the wheels.
The dealership remains owner and possessor, because ownership only passes on agreement and handover.
The dealership remains owner; until collection nobody is possessor.
§ 929 BGB: ownership passes by agreement and handover. Payment alone is not enough. Until handover the dealership has ownership and possession (actual control).
Autohaus Nordring GmbH uses general terms and conditions (AGB) for all workshop orders. Determine which statement about the AGB is correct.
AGB apply only to consumers and never to business customers.
AGB always take priority over terms negotiated individually with the customer.
AGB are pre-formulated contract terms that become part of the contract if the customer is referred to them when the contract is made and can reasonably take note of them.
If the AGB contain an invalid clause, the whole workshop contract is void.
AGB also become part of the contract if they are only sent with the invoice after the repair.

§ 305 BGB: AGB are included only with a reference and the chance to read them when the contract is made. Individual agreements take priority (§ 305b); an invalid clause leaves the rest of the contract valid (§ 306).
A customer bought a navigation device from Autohaus Nordring GmbH. After two weeks the display fails. Determine which right the customer must assert first.
She can withdraw from the contract at once and reclaim the price.
She must first demand subsequent performance and may choose between repair and delivery of a new device.
She can reduce the price at once without giving the dealership a chance to repair.
She must first demand subsequent performance, and the dealership always decides alone whether to repair or replace.
She no longer has any rights because she did not complain about the defect when buying.
§§ 437, 439 BGB: subsequent performance comes first, and the buyer chooses between repair and replacement. Withdrawal and price reduction only come into question if it fails.
Autohaus Nordring GmbH wants to shorten its liability for defects towards private customers. Determine which arrangement is legally permitted.
For new cars, the limitation period for defects may be shortened to one year by AGB.
For used cars, liability for defects may be excluded entirely if the customer signs the contract.
For used cars, the limitation period may be shortened to one year if this is agreed expressly and separately.
For new cars, the limitation period may be shortened to one year if the price is paid in cash.
Shortening is not possible for new or used vehicles; two years always apply.
§ 476 BGB: in consumer sales, two years apply compulsorily to new goods. For used goods, shortening to one year is only possible by express, separate agreement; exclusion is never allowed.
Autohaus Nordring GmbH finances a new vehicle lift with a bank loan. As security, ownership of the lift is transferred to the bank (Sicherungsübereignung). Determine which statement is correct.
The bank becomes possessor of the lift; the dealership remains owner.
The bank becomes owner of the lift; the dealership remains possessor and may continue to use it.
The dealership assigns its claims against workshop customers to the bank.
The lift is entered in the land register in favour of the bank.
The bank becomes owner and possessor; the dealership rents the lift back.

In a transfer of ownership by way of security, the bank receives security ownership; handover is replaced by a constructive possession agreement. The dealership remains possessor and keeps using the lift. Assigning claims is a Zession; the land register concerns charges on land.

The shareholders of Autohaus Nordring GmbH have made no provision on profit distribution in the articles. The annual profit of 120.000,00 € is to be paid out in full. Determine which statement is correct.
Each shareholder receives 40.000,00 € because profit is shared per head.
Each shareholder first receives 4 % of his share, the rest is shared per head.
Petra Lorenz receives 60.000,00 €, Jonas Lorenz 36.000,00 € and Mehmet Arslan 24.000,00 €.
The managing shareholder first receives a fee for her work, the rest is shared per head.
Profit is shared in a reasonable ratio decided by the managing directors alone.

§ 29 (3) GmbHG: without a provision in the articles, profit is shared in proportion to the shares: 150 : 90 : 60 = 50 % : 30 % : 20 %. The 4 % rule applies to the OHG, the 'reasonable' split to the KG.
Sabine Krüger holds sole Prokura at Autohaus Nordring GmbH. Determine which transaction she may not conclude effectively without special authorisation.
She takes out a loan of 200.000,00 € to buy demonstration cars.
She hires a vehicle mechatronics technician on a permanent contract.
She sells a company property of the GmbH that is no longer needed.
She grants an employee in the parts store general commercial authority.
She opens another business account at a different bank.

§ 49 HGB: Prokura covers all transactions that running any commercial business entails, including loans and hiring. Selling or charging land requires special authorisation. Not allowed at all are, for example, granting Prokura and signing the balance sheet.
Service manager Uwe Franke holds general commercial authority at Autohaus Nordring GmbH. Determine which transaction he may carry out effectively without special authority.
He takes out a loan to buy a wheel alignment system.
He conducts a lawsuit for the GmbH against a customer in default.
He orders spare parts and workshop materials for ongoing repairs.
He signs the purchase contract for a company property, adding 'ppa.'.
He grants Prokura to the workshop foreman.

§ 54 HGB: general commercial authority covers ordinary transactions of the business. Loans and lawsuits require special authority; land transactions and granting Prokura are excluded. Authorised agents sign 'i. V.', not 'ppa.'.

Autohaus Nordring GmbH wants to give warehouse employee Mr Sander ordinary notice. He has worked there for six years; no collective agreement with different periods applies. Use the extract to determine which statement is correct.
Notice can be given with four weeks to the 15th or the end of a calendar month.
The period is two months to the end of a month; if employment is to end on 30.06., notice must be received by 30.04. at the latest.
The period is two months to the end of a month; the decisive day is the day the notice is sent.
The extended periods apply in the same way if Mr Sander wants to resign himself.
The period is three months to the end of a quarter because Mr Sander has worked there for more than five years.

§ 622 (2) BGB: after five years of service the employer gives notice of two months to the end of a month. Receipt of the notice is decisive. The extended periods only apply to notice given by the employer.

Notice period

quiz: The regular works council election is due at Autohaus Nordring GmbH. Determine which statement informs the staff correctly.
Regular works council elections take place every five years between 1 March and 31 August.
All employees aged 16 or over may vote; all adult employees may be elected regardless of how long they have worked there.
Regular works council elections take place every four years between 1 March and 31 May.
Only the trade unions represented in the company may submit nominations.
Trainees are excluded from the works council election because they elect the youth and trainee representation.

§ 13 BetrVG: every four years from 1 March to 31 May. Employees aged 16 and over, including trainees, may vote (§ 7); anyone who is of age and has worked there for at least six months may be elected (§ 8). Employees may also submit nominations.
Trainee Jana Petersen falls off her bicycle on the direct way from home to vocational school and breaks her arm. Determine which statement is correct.
It is a private accident; only her health insurance fund is responsible.
It is a commuting accident; statutory accident insurance is responsible, and its contributions are paid by the employer alone.
It is a commuting accident; statutory accident insurance is responsible, and employer and trainee each pay half of its contributions.
The accident is not insured because the way to vocational school is not a way to work.
The training company's business liability insurance is responsible.
The direct way to vocational school is also insured by statutory accident insurance (Berufsgenossenschaft). Its contributions are paid by the employer alone.
After a pay rise, the gross salary of the sales manager of Autohaus Nordring GmbH is above the contribution ceiling of statutory pension insurance. Determine the consequence.
He is no longer compulsorily insured in statutory pension insurance and must make private provision.
No pension contributions are charged on the part of his salary above the contribution ceiling.
In future he must also pay the employer's share of pension contributions himself.
He must switch from statutory to private health insurance.
A higher contribution rate applies to the part of his salary above the ceiling.

Contributions are only calculated up to the contribution ceiling. Compulsory pension insurance continues. Switching to private health insurance depends on the health insurance threshold and is never compulsory.
An employee of Autohaus Nordring GmbH has had a monthly allowance for wage tax deduction registered because of high travel costs. Determine the effect of the allowance.
Monthly wage tax falls by exactly the amount of the allowance.
The employer pays the allowance in addition to gross pay.
Wage tax is calculated on pay reduced by the allowance; social security contributions stay the same.
Neither wage tax nor social security contributions are charged on the amount of the allowance.
The allowance only takes effect after the income tax return in the following year.
An allowance reduces the wage tax base already in the monthly deduction. Tax therefore only falls by the tax attributable to it. Social security is still calculated on full gross pay.
Employee Ms Yilmaz wants to claim income-related expenses (Werbungskosten) in her income tax return. Determine which expense counts as income-related.
church tax paid in the previous year
premiums for her private liability insurance
a donation to a non-profit sports club
journeys between home and first place of work
co-payments for medicines after a long illness

Income-related expenses serve to earn, secure and maintain income, e.g. commuting or trade union fees. Church tax, donations and insurance premiums are special expenses; medical costs are extraordinary burdens.
On a perfect market for winter tyres, the model of supply and demand applies. Determine in which case the equilibrium price falls, all other conditions remaining the same.
Demand rises, supply stays the same.
Supply falls, demand stays the same.
Supply and demand rise by the same amount.
Supply rises, demand stays the same.
Demand rises more strongly than supply.
If supply rises with unchanged demand, the supply curve shifts to the right: the equilibrium price falls and the quantity sold rises. If both rise equally, the price stays the same.
A market research institute has determined the data shown for a small car model. Determine which statement is correct.
At a price of 20.000 € there is excess demand of 300 vehicles.
At a price of 20.000 € there is excess supply of 300 vehicles; the price will tend to fall.
At a price of 18.000 € there is excess supply of 250 vehicles.
The equilibrium price is 21.000 € because most is supplied there.
At a price of 17.000 € the most is sold because demand is highest there.

At 20.000 € 750 vehicles are supplied but only 450 demanded: excess supply of 300, the price comes under pressure. At 18.000 € there is excess demand. The equilibrium price is 19.000 € (600 = 600); the most is sold there.

Cell 4: supply oligopoly
Cell 6: supply oligopoly
Cell 6: demand oligopoly
Cell 8: polypoly
Cell 3: supply monopoly
Few sellers and many buyers form a supply oligopoly: row 'few sellers', column 'many buyers', i.e. cell 6. Cell 9 would be a polypoly, cell 3 a supply monopoly.

quiz: The social market economy shapes Germany's economic order. Determine in which case three features of this economic order are named.
Collective ownership of means of production – free collective bargaining – decentralised planning
Private ownership of means of production – freedom of association – central planning of production
Free collective bargaining – social obligation of property – redistribution by the state
State price setting for all goods – free choice of occupation – protection of competition
Freedom of trade – freedom of contract – no state social policy at all

The social market economy combines private property and competition with social balance: free collective bargaining, the social obligation of property (Art. 14 GG) and redistribution via taxes and benefits. Collective ownership, central planning and state prices belong to a planned economy; no social policy belongs to a pure market economy.
The economic policy goals of the Stability and Growth Act are shown as the 'magic square'. Determine in which case the four goals are named correctly.
Price stability, high level of employment, external equilibrium, steady and appropriate economic growth
Wage stability, high level of employment, balanced state budget, steady economic growth
Price stability, full employment, fair income distribution, environmental protection
Exchange rate stability, high level of employment, external equilibrium, maximum economic growth
Price stability, low level of employment, external surplus, steady economic growth
§ 1 StabG: price stability, high employment, external equilibrium and steady, appropriate growth. Fair income distribution and environmental protection extend the square to the magic hexagon.
A press release says: 'Real gross domestic product rose by 0,8 % year on year, nominal GDP by 3,1 %.' Determine which statement is correct.
The quantity of goods and services produced rose as strongly as nominal GDP.
Prices rose on average by exactly the real growth.
Much of the nominal increase is due to price rises; adjusted for prices the economy grew much more weakly.
Unlike nominal GDP, real GDP also includes residents' income from abroad.
Real GDP is valued at current-year prices, nominal GDP at previous-year prices.

Real means price-adjusted (at previous-year prices), nominal means at current prices. The gap between nominal and real growth is mainly due to price rises. Income from abroad concerns national income, not the real/nominal difference.
Autohaus Nordring GmbH wants to recognise early whether an economic upswing is coming. Decide which indicator is a leading indicator.
the unemployment rate
the development of collectively agreed wages
the state's tax revenue
incoming orders in industry and companies' business expectations
the number of company insolvencies
Leading indicators run ahead of the economy, e.g. incoming orders or the business climate. Unemployment, agreed wages, tax revenue and insolvencies react later (lagging indicators).
The figure shows a simplified business cycle. Determine which description is typical for point C.
Companies' capacities are fully used; prices and wages rise strongly.
Incoming orders fall, short-time work increases and companies invest less.
Incoming orders rise, companies hire again and the mood improves.
Unemployment is very low and there is a shortage of skilled workers.
Interest rates and prices rise strongly because demand exceeds supply.
C lies in the downswing (recession): demand and orders fall, short-time work increases, investment drops. A = upswing, B = boom, D = trough.

f.cap: Development of real GDP (index)

quiz: The economy is in a downswing. Determine which measure by the federal government is suitable, as anti-cyclical fiscal policy, to support aggregate demand.
raising income tax rates
cutting public construction contracts
improving depreciation allowances for investment
building an economic equalisation reserve from extra tax revenue
abolishing investment grants

In a downswing the state should stimulate demand: more public contracts, tax cuts, better depreciation, investment grants. Tax rises, cuts and building an equalisation reserve dampen demand and belong in a boom.
To maintain price stability, the European Central Bank (ECB) uses monetary policy instruments. Determine which measure is intended to reduce the money supply in the euro area.
The ECB lowers the rate for main refinancing operations.
The ECB buys government bonds from commercial banks.
The ECB lowers the minimum reserve ratio.
The ECB sells securities to commercial banks.
The ECB grants commercial banks additional long-term loans.
When the ECB sells securities, central bank money flows back from the banks to the ECB: the money supply falls. Rate cuts, securities purchases, a lower reserve ratio and extra loans increase it.
The state makes various payments. Determine which payment is a transfer payment to private households.
the salary of a civil-servant vocational school teacher
payment to a craft business for renovating a school
child benefit for a family with two children
a subsidy for a manufacturer of electric vehicles
interest on a federal bond held by a saver

Transfer payments are payments to private households without direct consideration, e.g. child benefit. Salary and contract payments pay for services, subsidies go to companies, interest is capital income.
There are various forms of cooperation and concentration on the market for vehicle parts. Determine which statement is NOT correct.
In a cartel, legally and economically independent companies agree on prices, for example; such agreements are prohibited in principle.
In a group (Konzern) the companies remain legally independent but are under uniform management.
In a merger, companies combine into one; at least one loses its legal independence.
In a group, the companies involved always keep their economic independence.
In a purchasing association, the dealerships involved keep their legal independence.
In a group the companies lose their economic independence (uniform management) but keep their legal independence. Cartels are prohibited in principle under § 1 GWB.
23-year-old trainee Felix Brandt has been at Autohaus Nordring GmbH for seven months. He wants to give up the training to start a degree. Determine which statement is correct.
After the probation period he can only resign without notice for good cause.
He can resign with four weeks' notice; the notice must be in writing and state the reason.
He can resign orally with two weeks' notice.
He can resign at any time without notice and without giving reasons.
He cannot resign, only conclude a termination agreement with the consent of the IHK.

§ 22 (2) no. 2 and (3) BBiG: after probation the trainee may resign with four weeks' notice if he gives up the training or wants to learn another occupation, in writing and stating the reason. Without notice and reason is only possible during probation.
Which costs are typical direct costs at a dealership?
Showroom rent
Cost price of a new car
Accountant's salary
Electricity costs
Directly attributable to the vehicle.
Imputed entrepreneur's salary is part of …
basic costs
different costs
additional costs
neutral expenses
Costs with no corresponding expense.
What is the base for the workshop overhead rate?
Revenue
Productive wages
Fixed assets
Number of employees
The workshop's direct costs are productive wages.
The short-term price floor is at the …
full cost
variable unit costs
fixed unit costs
direct costs plus profit
Contribution margin equals zero.
In cost accounting, a donation to the Red Cross is …
basic costs
additional costs
non-operational (neutral) expense
direct costs
No connection to the business purpose.
What does a level 1 liquidity of 20 % tell you?
20 % of assets are liquid
Cash covers 20 % of short-term debts
20 % of revenue is profit
Equity covers 20 % of fixed assets
Cash / short-term debt.
A used car is bought from a private seller and sold under margin taxation. VAT is due on …
the selling price
the purchase price
the difference between selling and purchase price
nothing
§ 25a UStG.
Which booking belongs to the withdrawal from stock of a sold new car?
8000 Revenue new cars to 3000 New car stock
7000 VAK new cars to 3000 New car stock
3000 New car stock to 7000 VAK new cars
1400 Trade receivables to 3000 New car stock
With the sale the car leaves stock and becomes an expense: 7000 VAK new cars (cost of sales) on the debit side to 3000 New car stock on the credit side.
Lease for a parking area belongs to account …
0050 Land
2300 Other expenses
4400 Rent, lease
2100 Interest expense
Ongoing expense and cost, not fixed assets.
An authorised dealer sells new cars …
in the name and for the account of the manufacturer
in its own name and for its own account
in its own name for the account of the manufacturer
only as a broker
Independent trader.
In the genuine agency model, the sales risk is borne by …
the dealership
the manufacturer
the bank
the customer
The agent only brokers.
How long is a private customer bound by a binding order for a car not in stock?
10 days
2 weeks
3 weeks
6 weeks
New car sales conditions: 3 weeks.
The reversal of the burden of proof in consumer sales applies for …
6 months
12 months
24 months
not at all for vehicles
Since 2022: 12 months.
A collision with game is covered by …
liability
partial cover
only comprehensive cover
passenger accident insurance
Partial cover.
Under German commercial law (HGB, standard leasing), how does leasing affect the lessee's balance sheet?
Fixed assets and debt rise
No effect on fixed assets and debt
Equity rises
Fixed assets fall
It is capitalised by the lessor.
What is the final instalment of three-way financing based on?
the list price
the expected residual value
the down payment
the interest rate
Expected value at the end of the term.
Which document stays with the seller under retention of title?
Registration certificate part I
Registration certificate part II
Service book
CoC
Registration certificate part II.
The state pays manufacturers of wall boxes for electric cars a grant for each wall box sold. Determine how this subsidy affects the market for wall boxes, all other conditions remaining the same.
The demand curve shifts to the right; price and quantity rise.
The supply curve shifts to the right; the equilibrium price falls and the quantity rises.
The supply curve shifts to the left; the equilibrium price rises.
A state maximum price below the equilibrium price arises.
The demand curve shifts to the left because buyers wait for further grants.
The subsidy lowers suppliers' costs: they offer more at every price, so the supply curve shifts to the right. The equilibrium price falls and the quantity sold rises.
Because rents are rising sharply, a city is considering setting a state maximum price for flats. Determine which statement is correct.
A maximum price only works if it is above the equilibrium price; it mainly protects suppliers.
An effective maximum price is below the equilibrium price and leads to excess demand.
An effective maximum price is below the equilibrium price and leads to excess supply.
A maximum price always equals the equilibrium price and therefore does not change the market.
A maximum price leads to more flats being offered because landlords have secure income.

Maximum prices are meant to protect buyers and lie below the equilibrium price. There, more is demanded than supplied: excess demand, e.g. waiting lists or a black market. Minimum prices lie above it and lead to excess supply.
Determine which description characterises the used car market as an imperfect market.
Buyers and sellers are always fully informed about all offers and prices.
Anyone who wants to sell or buy used cars can do so freely.
Many buyers prefer a particular dealership because of friendly advice and a short journey.
The vehicles offered are completely identical.
All market participants react immediately to every price change.

A market is imperfect if at least one condition of the perfect market is missing, e.g. because buyers have personal or spatial preferences. The other statements describe conditions of a perfect market.
Two dealerships of the same brand in neighbouring towns merge into one company. Determine how this combination is described.
vertical combination, because the companies work at different economic stages
horizontal combination, because the companies work at the same economic stage
diagonal combination, because the companies work in different industries
vertical combination, because both companies sell vehicles of the same manufacturer
cartel, because both companies remain legally independent

Horizontal: same economic stage (retail and retail). Vertical: upstream and downstream stages (e.g. manufacturer and dealer). Diagonal: different industries. Companies that merge into one do not stay independent.
Two large car retail groups want to merge. Determine which statement on merger control is correct.
The merger must be approved by the Deutsche Bundesbank because loans are affected.
The competent IHK checks whether training places will be lost and can prohibit the merger.
The Federal Cartel Office checks whether the merger would significantly impede effective competition and can prohibit it.
Mergers are prohibited in principle in Germany and only allowed with the consent of the Bundestag.
The Federal Statistical Office checks market shares and grants permission to merge.
Large mergers must be notified to the Federal Cartel Office (§§ 35 ff. GWB). It prohibits them if effective competition would be significantly impeded, in particular by a dominant position.
There are interactions between the goals of the magic square. Determine between which goals there is typically a conflict.
steady economic growth and a high level of employment
a high level of employment and price stability
price stability and preserving the purchasing power of money
steady economic growth and rising state tax revenue
environmental protection and better air quality in cities

High employment raises income and demand; this can drive up wages and prices (conflict). Growth and employment, price stability and purchasing power, and growth and tax revenue support each other (harmony).
You have the data shown from a country's national accounts. Determine which statement is correct.
The data belong to the production approach because they show in which sectors GDP was generated.
The data belong to the expenditure approach; net exports are positive because more was exported than imported.
The data belong to the income approach because they show how income is split between labour and capital.
The data belong to the expenditure approach; net exports are negative because imports are deducted from GDP.
The data belong to the balance of payments because exports and imports are listed.
Expenditure approach: private consumption + government consumption + gross investment + net exports (exports − imports). Here net exports are positive at 160 bn €; GDP is 4.050 bn €.
