quiz: For several years the inflation rate has been clearly above interest rates on savings and loans. Determine who usually benefits from this development.
savers, because their balances still earn interest
pensioners with a fixed company pension, because it is paid regularly
borrowers with fixed interest rates, because their debts lose value in real terms
creditors, because they can demand higher interest on existing contracts
employees with wages fixed for the long term, because their purchasing power rises
Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money. Those with fixed-rate debts repay less in real terms. Savers, creditors and people on fixed incomes lose purchasing power.
Determine which statement about the mandate and position of the European Central Bank (ECB) is correct.
The ECB's primary goal is full employment in the euro area; it is bound by instructions of the EU Commission.
The ECB's primary goal is price stability; it aims for inflation of 2 % in the medium term and is independent of government instructions.
The ECB's primary goal is the highest possible euro exchange rate so that imports become cheap.
The ECB finances member states' budget deficits through direct loans to governments.
The ECB sets VAT rates in the euro area to keep prices stable.
Art. 127 TFEU: the primary goal is price stability; the ECB aims for 2 % inflation in the medium term. It is independent and may not finance states directly. Taxes are set by the states.
The extended circular flow distinguishes private households, companies, the state, banks (wealth formation) and the rest of the world. Determine which statement is correct.
Households' savings flow to the banks and are passed on from there as loans for investment by companies.
Households pay subsidies to the state; the state pays taxes to companies.
Companies receive factor income from households in the form of wages and rents.
Exports cause money to flow from home to abroad.
Households' savings flow directly to companies as consumer spending.

Saving flows to the banks (wealth formation) and finances companies' investment. Factor income flows from companies to households, subsidies from the state to companies; with exports money flows from abroad into the country.
Determine which statement about Germany's balance of payments is correct.
The trade balance is part of the financial account and records direct investment abroad.
The trade balance is part of the current account and records exports and imports of goods.
The services balance records exports of goods, e.g. new cars.
The balance of payments is part of the balance sheet of an exporting car maker.
Spending by German tourists abroad is recorded in the trade balance.
The current account comprises the trade balance (goods), the services balance (e.g. travel), primary and secondary income. Capital flows such as direct investment are in the financial account.
A product makes a loss on a full-cost basis, its contribution margin is positive. In the short term, you should …
drop it immediately
keep it in the range
only sell it below variable costs
give it away
It helps cover fixed costs.
At the break-even point:
Revenue = variable costs
Revenue = total costs
Contribution margin = 0
Fixed costs = 0
Neither profit nor loss.
The leverage effect is positive when …
the interest on debt is above the return on total capital
the return on total capital is above the interest on debt
there is no debt
liquidity is above 100 %
Then debt earns more than it costs.
Imputed depreciation is calculated from the …
acquisition value
replacement value
book value
scrap value
The replacement purchase should be earned through prices.
Which cost centre is a service cost centre at a dealership?
Workshop
New cars
Administration
Parts and accessories
It is allocated to the main cost centres.
A workshop index of 3,85 means:
3,85 % profit
For each 1 € of productive wages, 3,85 € labour revenue must be earned
The workshop is 38,5 % utilised
385 € hourly rate
Target labour revenue / productive wages.
Which allocation key fits rent?
Revenue
Floor space in m²
Number of employees
Asset values
By cause, according to space used.
The golden balance sheet rule requires that …
current assets are financed with equity
fixed assets are financed long term
there are no debts
level 1 liquidity is 100 %
Matching maturities of assets and capital.
Which sales form sells new cars in the name and for the account of the manufacturer?
Authorised dealer
Agency
Service partner
Independent dealer
The agent only brokers.
A manufacturer only admits dealers who meet its standards. That is a … distribution system.
exclusive
selective
direct
open
Selection by fixed criteria.
Determine which statement about founding and registering a GmbH such as Autohaus Nordring GmbH is correct.
The GmbH comes into being when the articles are signed; registration in the commercial register is only declaratory.
The GmbH only comes into being as a legal person on registration in section B of the commercial register; registration is constitutive.
The GmbH is registered in section A because it carries on a commercial business.
The articles of a GmbH only need written form.
Before registration, the persons acting are not liable because the GmbH does not exist yet.

§ 11 GmbHG: before registration the GmbH does not exist as such; registration in section B is constitutive. The articles must be notarised, and anyone who acts in the GmbH's name before registration is personally liable.
Determine which statement about the commercial register is correct.
Section A contains sole traders and partnerships such as OHG and KG; section B contains corporations such as GmbH and AG.
Section A contains corporations; section B contains all other merchants.
The commercial register is kept by the chamber of commerce (IHK) and is not public.
An OHG is entered in the land register because its partners are liable with their private assets.
Registration of a merchant by trade (Istkaufmann) is always constitutive.
Section A: registered merchants, OHG, KG. Section B: GmbH, UG, AG. The register is kept electronically by the local court and is public. For an Istkaufmann registration is declaratory.
Determine which statement about merchant status is correct.
Autohaus Nordring GmbH is a Kannkaufmann because it can register voluntarily.
Autohaus Nordring GmbH is a Formkaufmann because it is a merchant solely by virtue of its legal form.
A small trader without a commercially organised business is always an Istkaufmann.
A farmer is always a merchant by law, even without registration.
Autohaus Nordring GmbH is not a merchant because it is a legal person.

§ 6 HGB: corporations are merchants by legal form (Formkaufleute). An Istkaufmann runs a commercial business with a commercially organised operation. Small traders, farmers and foresters may register voluntarily (Kannkaufleute).
Determine in which case only partnerships are named.
GmbH – KG – OHG
OHG – KG – GbR
AG – UG (limited liability) – KG
OHG – AG – registered cooperative
GmbH – UG (limited liability) – AG
Partnerships are the GbR, OHG and KG (including the GmbH & Co. KG). GmbH, UG and AG are corporations; the eG is a cooperative.
Autohaus Nordring GmbH distributes brochures with prices for summer wheels. A customer asks for wheels at the brochure price, but they are sold out. Determine which statement is correct.
The brochure is a binding offer; the dealership must obtain the wheels.
The brochure is an invitation to make an offer; only the customer's order is the offer.
The brochure is the acceptance of an offer the customer makes by coming in.
A purchase contract was concluded when the customer came in, because the price was fixed.
The brochure is binding because it was distributed in writing.
Brochures, catalogues and window displays are aimed at the public; they are invitations to make an offer. The customer's order is the offer, which the dealership can accept or reject.
An employee of Autohaus Nordring GmbH offers a supplier on the phone to buy 40 batteries at a certain price. The supplier wants to reply the next day. Determine which statement is correct.
The offer binds the dealership for one week.
The offer must be accepted immediately during the call; acceptance the next day counts as a new offer.
The offer is valid until the end of the month because it was made by a merchant.
The offer is not binding because it was only made orally.
If the supplier stays silent, the offer counts as accepted after three days.

§ 147 BGB: an offer between persons present, including by phone, can only be accepted immediately. Late acceptance counts as a new offer (§ 150 BGB). Oral offers are binding; silence is generally not acceptance.
A written offer from Autohaus Nordring GmbH for roof boxes contains the addition 'while stocks last'. Determine the effect of this addition.
The offer is completely non-binding, including the price.
The commitment to the delivery quantity is limited; price and other terms remain binding.
The price becomes non-binding; the quantity remains binding.
The addition is not permitted and makes the offer void.
The addition extends the binding period until all roof boxes are sold.
'While stocks last' is an exemption clause that only concerns the quantity. 'Freibleibend' or 'non-binding' would make the whole offer non-binding, 'price subject to change' only the price.
The law prescribes a special form for certain transactions. Determine which transaction is only valid if notarised.
buying a used car at a high price
giving notice on an employment contract
the purchase contract for land for a new showroom
a consumer loan agreement to finance a new car
registering an OHG in the commercial register
§ 311b BGB: land purchase contracts must be notarised, otherwise they are void. Notice and consumer loans require written form; commercial register applications require public certification.
Autohaus Nordring GmbH ordered 100 sets of brake pads. 100 sets are delivered and invoiced, but the box contains only 80. Determine which type of defect exists.
defect in kind (wrong delivery)
defect in quantity (short delivery)
defect in quality because the goods are unusable
assembly defect because the pads still have to be fitted
no defect but a delay in delivery, because the rest can be delivered later
Delivering less than agreed is a defect: the agreed characteristics also include the quantity (§ 434 (2) BGB).
A supplier of Autohaus Nordring GmbH does not deliver ordered tyres on time. Determine which requirements must be met for a delay in delivery.
The goods are defective and the buyer has already paid.
Delivery is due, the supplier has received a reminder (unless the date was fixed by the calendar) and he is responsible for the delay.
Delivery is due; a reminder is never needed and fault does not matter.
Delivery is delayed by force majeure, e.g. a natural disaster.
The buyer set a grace period and then withdrew from the contract.

Delay in delivery (§ 286 BGB): due date, reminder (not needed for a calendar date) and fault of the supplier. With force majeure there is no fault. Grace period and withdrawal are rights arising from the delay, not requirements.
Because of a delay in delivery, Autohaus Nordring GmbH buys the tyres from another dealer at a higher price (cover purchase). Determine which statement is correct.
The extra cost is an abstract loss that can only be recovered through a contractual penalty.
The extra cost is a concrete loss that the GmbH can claim as damages from the defaulting supplier.
The extra cost is a non-material loss that is not compensated.
A cover purchase is only permitted if the defaulting supplier agreed beforehand.
The extra cost is only compensated if the supplier acted intentionally.

The extra cost of a cover purchase can be proven exactly (concrete loss) and is recoverable as damages in lieu of performance. An abstract loss is only estimated, e.g. lost profit. Negligence is sufficient.
Daily usage 12 units, delivery time 5 days, minimum stock 40 units. The reorder point is …
60 units
100 units
52 units
200 units
At the optimal order quantity …
storage costs are lowest
ordering costs are lowest
ordering and storage costs together are lowest
cost prices are highest
Minimum of total costs.
Which storage principle suits tyres and batteries that age?
LiFo
FiFo
chaotic storage
just-in-time
Sell older goods first.
The supplier collects varying amounts from the account each month. That is …
a standing order
a direct debit
a bank transfer
a cheque
Amount and date can vary.
Payment term 30 days, 2 % cash discount if paid within 10 days. The supplier credit costs per year about …
The dealership adds roof boxes as a new product group. The range becomes …
deeper
wider
shallower
narrower
New product group: width.
Wiper blades from another manufacturer are added to the existing ones. The range becomes …
wider
deeper
narrower
shallower
More choice within the product group.
„Would you like the alloy wheels in silver or black?“ is …
an open question
an alternative question
a rhetorical question
a leading question
Two options to choose from.
„You like the winter tyres better too, don't you?“ is …
an open question
a checking question
a leading question
an alternative question
The answer is suggested.
What directly follows the greeting in a sales conversation?
Sales arguments
Needs analysis
Closing
Product demonstration
First find out what the customer needs.
What is the order of customer-oriented arguments?
Benefit, feature, advantage
Feature, advantage, benefit
Advantage, benefit, feature
Price, feature, benefit
From the product to the customer.
Which shelf zone sells best?
Bend zone
Stretch zone
Eye level zone
Base zone
Goods at eye level.
What is non-verbal communication?
a friendly greeting with words
a smile
price information
a question
Body language.
Accident not your fault: which claim does the injured party have only in a liability case, not with comprehensive cover?
Repair costs
Reduction in market value
Glass breakage
Deductible
Comprehensive cover only pays according to contract.
Replacement value 10.000 €. Up to which repair costs may the car be repaired under the 130 % rule?
The customer is entitled to deduct input VAT. The other party's insurer pays the repair …
gross
net
not at all
half
He reclaims the VAT from the tax office.
With the assignment by way of security (RKÜ) …
the customer waives damages
the customer assigns their claim against the insurer to the dealership
the dealership accepts blame for the accident
the deductible is waived
The dealership invoices directly.
The keeper is liable for the operating risk of their vehicle even without fault. This is called …
fault-based liability
strict liability
product liability
guarantee
Reason for compulsory insurance.
A used car invoice says „VAT deductible“. The vehicle is …
margin-taxed
standard-taxed
tax-exempt
a re-import
Full VAT on the net price.
The overpayment on a trade-in (hidden price discount) is borne by …
the used car department
the new car department
the workshop
the manufacturer
It served the new car sale.
Capacity to borrow means …
sufficient income
full legal capacity
no SCHUFA entries
own securities
The legal ability to conclude loan contracts.
With an absolute guarantee (selbstschuldnerische Bürgschaft) …
the guarantor is only liable after unsuccessful enforcement
the bank can claim against the guarantor immediately
the guarantor is not liable at all
the guarantor is only liable for interest
No defence of prior enforcement.
With an annuity loan …
the instalment keeps falling
the instalment stays the same, the repayment share rises
repayment is only at the end
the interest share rises
Interest share falls with the outstanding balance.
The tender right (Andienungsrecht) in leasing means:
The lessee may buy the vehicle
The lessor can oblige the lessee to buy
The dealer must take back the vehicle
The contract is extended
A right of the lessor.
By when must motor insurance be cancelled regularly at year end?
31 October
30 November
15 December
31 December
One month before expiry.
A qualified job reference additionally contains …
the salary
information on performance and conduct
the reasons for dismissal
days absent
The simple reference only states type and duration.
How long is maternity protection after a normal birth?
6 weeks
8 weeks
12 weeks
4 months
6 weeks before, 8 weeks after.
What break does the Working Hours Act require for more than 6 to 9 hours of work?
15 minutes
30 minutes
45 minutes
60 minutes
Over 9 hours: 45 minutes.
Before a conduct-related dismissal, the following is usually required:
a social selection
a formal warning
a termination agreement
IHK approval
It warns and gives the chance to change.
What is not a criterion for social selection?
Age
Maintenance obligations
Performance last year
Length of service
Severe disability also counts.
To whom does the employer pay social security contributions?
to the tax office
to the health insurance fund
directly to the pension insurance
to the employment agency
The health insurance fund is the collection agency.
Gross list price of a company car with a combustion engine 40.000 €. Taxable benefit for private use under the 1 % method per month:
1 % of the gross list price rounded down to full 100 €.
Several collective agreements of the motor trade apply to Autohaus Nordring GmbH. Determine which matter is typically regulated in a framework agreement (Manteltarifvertrag).
the level of hourly wages and trainee pay for the coming year
the assignment of activities to pay grades
general working conditions such as working hours, holidays, bonuses and notice periods
the timing of breaks in the workshop of Autohaus Nordring GmbH
interest on employer loans to staff

The framework agreement regulates general working conditions for the long term. Pay levels are in the wage and salary agreement, grading in the pay framework agreement. Breaks in an individual company are set by a works agreement.
A vehicle mechatronics technician at Autohaus Nordring GmbH fears that a back condition will stop him working in his job until retirement. Determine which insurance best covers his loss of income.
private liability insurance
statutory accident insurance, because it pays for every illness
private occupational disability insurance
household contents insurance
statutory unemployment insurance, because it pays permanently in case of occupational disability

Occupational disability insurance pays a pension if the last job can no longer be done. The statutory reduced earning capacity pension is much lower; accident insurance only pays for work and commuting accidents and recognised occupational diseases.
Trainee Mia Schulz has only low income-related expenses in the year. Determine which statement about the employee lump sum is correct.
It is only taken into account if Mia proves her expenses individually with receipts.
It is deducted without proof if the actual expenses are lower; it amounts to 1.230 € a year.
It amounts to 12.348 € and exempts the subsistence minimum from tax.
It only applies to employees who travel more than 20 kilometres to work.
It is deducted in addition to the expenses actually proven.
The employee lump sum of 1.230 € is deducted without proof. Itemising only pays off if actual expenses are higher; you cannot have both. 12.348 € is the basic tax-free allowance for 2026.
Which values are determined by book stocktaking?
New car stock
Spare parts in stock
Receivables and bank balances
Tools
Not physically tangible, so from documents.
With shifted stocktaking, counting may take place …
only on the balance sheet date
up to 3 months before or 2 months after the reporting date
at any time during the year
only every 3 years
With roll-forward or roll-back to the reporting date.
A part was bought for 100 € and is worth 80 € on the reporting date. Recognised is …
Lower of cost or market principle.
Net worth is …
fixed assets + current assets
assets − debts
current assets − short-term debts
equity + debt
It equals equity.
A cash withdrawal from the bank account for the till is …
a liability exchange
an asset exchange
an increase on both sides
a decrease on both sides
Only asset accounts, the balance sheet total stays the same.
Buying spare parts on credit causes …
an increase on both sides
a decrease on both sides
a liability exchange
an asset exchange
Stock and payables rise.
On which side is the opening balance of a liability account?
debit
credit
both sides
it is not booked
Liability accounts increase on the credit side.
Which transaction affects profit?
Buying a car on credit
Transferring the rent
Cash withdrawal
Repaying a loan
An expense account is involved.
Via which account are expense and income accounts closed?
Closing balance sheet account
P&L account
Cash
Opening balance sheet account
The balance goes to equity.
Output VAT 9.500 €, input VAT 6.200 €. What is the VAT payable?
Output VAT − input VAT.
Why doesn't VAT reduce the dealership's profit?
because it is too low
because it is a transitory item
because it is only due the following year
because the manufacturer bears it
It is borne by the end consumer.
Which revenue is VAT-exempt?
Sale of accessories
Workshop labour
Brokering an insurance policy
Sale of a new car
Insurance revenue is tax-exempt.
A model with a high market share in a barely growing market is in the portfolio …
a star
a cash cow
a question mark
a poor dog
It brings money with little need for investment.
Market volume is …
the maximum possible sales
the actual sales of all suppliers
your own sales
the manufacturer's revenue
Market potential is the upper limit.
Which commission rewards the salesperson for giving little discount?
Revenue commission
Gross profit commission
Unit bonus
Fixed salary
Discount reduces gross profit and thus the commission.
The new car purchase contract is concluded through …
the test drive
the offer in the brochure
the acceptance in text form or delivery within the binding period
the down payment
The order is only the offer.
On the official registration fee, the dealership charges the customer …
19 % VAT
7 % VAT
no VAT
margin taxation
Transitory item.
An internal order is, for example, …
an inspection for a customer
the workshop reconditioning one of the dealership's own used cars
warranty work
accident damage
Service for an own department, without VAT.
What is the minimum liability for defects of a dealer selling a used car to a consumer?
6 months
1 year
2 years
none
Shortening from 2 years to 1 year is allowed if the consumer was specifically informed and it is agreed expressly and separately (§ 476 (2) BGB).
Which detail is mandatory on a new car invoice?
Colour of the vehicle
The dealership's tax number or VAT ID
Name of the responsible sales adviser
Mileage
Mandatory under VAT law.
A dealership has 3.000.000 € revenue and 45.000 € profit. What is the return on sales?
Return on sales = profit / revenue × 100 = 45.000 / 3.000.000 × 100 = 1,5 %.
A town has 200.000 inhabitants, there are 500 cars per 1.000 inhabitants. What is the „Kfz-Potenzial“ (vehicle potential)?
10.000 cars
40.000 cars
100.000 cars are registered in the market area, the useful life is 5 years. What is the annual replacement demand for new cars?
„Kfz-Potenzial“ / useful life = 100.000 / 5 = 20.000 new cars per year.
In which phase of the product life cycle do sales reach their peak?
Growth phase
Maturity phase
Introduction phase
Decline phase
Sales are highest in the maturity phase, followed by saturation and decline.
A supplier sends an unsolicited catalogue with prices. Legally, this is …
an enquiry
an advertisement (invitation to make an offer)
a binding offer
an order
Catalogues are aimed at the general public and are not binding.
The dealership orders in time on the basis of a binding offer. This means …
the supplier still has to send an order confirmation
the purchase contract has been concluded
only a preliminary contract has been concluded
the supplier can still refuse
Offer and timely acceptance make the purchase contract.
Which check takes place immediately on delivery with the driver present?
function test of the parts
check of packaging, number of packages and address
comparison with the incoming invoice
quality test in a laboratory
Visible external damage is confirmed on the delivery note.
Between merchants, an obvious defect is only reported after three weeks. Consequence:
full warranty rights
The rights are lost, the goods are deemed accepted
only a price reduction is possible
the deadline starts again
§ 377 HGB requires prompt notice of defects.
Instead of 20 brake discs of one type, 20 of another type are delivered. This is …
a defect in quantity
a wrong delivery
an installation error
no defect
Wrong goods are a wrong delivery. Legally it counts as a defect (§ 434 (5) BGB).
A firmly agreed delivery date („delivery on 15 March fixed“) is missed. The supplier is …
only in default after a reminder
in default immediately
never in default
only in default if intentional
With a calendar date, no reminder is needed.
Which source is suitable for finding new suppliers?
supplier database
trade fairs and online trade directories
stock card file
customer file
The supplier database only contains known suppliers.
In a qualitative comparison of offers, besides the price, what counts for example is …
only the list price
delivery time, quality and reliability
the number of employees
the legal form of the supplier
It is often done with a weighted scoring table.
With the order cycle method, orders are placed …
when the reorder point is reached
on fixed dates
only for customer orders
when the maximum stock is reached
With the reorder point method, you order at the reorder level.
The minimum stock (safety stock) serves to …
save storage costs
cover delivery delays and extra consumption
lower the maximum stock
get volume discounts
It may only be used in an emergency.
What is the effect of a higher turnover rate?
The storage period increases
Less capital is tied up, storage costs fall
The minimum stock increases
Storage interest rises
The goods spend less time in the warehouse.
With chaotic storage (free location system) …
every item has a fixed place
every free space is used, the computer remembers the location
no stocktaking takes place
there is no warehouse management
This saves space but needs good warehouse management.
Which storage costs are capital costs?
rent for the warehouse
interest on the money tied up in stock
wages of warehouse staff
electricity
The tied-up capital could otherwise earn interest.
The incoming invoice shows a 10 % discount, 15 % was agreed. What do you do?
pay the invoice anyway
raise the discrepancy with the supplier and have the invoice corrected
send the goods back
deduct the discount yourself without saying anything
Incoming invoices are checked against the order and delivery note.
In a sales conversation, „finding out customer wishes“ mainly means:
stating the price
needs analysis with open questions
closing the sale
complaint
Open questions get the customer talking.
A customer says: „That's too expensive for me.“ A suitable reaction is …
give a discount immediately
explain the benefit in relation to the price (value for money)
end the conversation
contradict the customer
Take objections seriously and argue with the benefit.
In the showroom, accessories are best presented so that …
they are behind the counter
customers can see them, touch them and link them to the vehicle
only price tags are visible
they stay in the warehouse
Themed presentation, e.g. winter season with tyres and chains.
General terms and conditions become part of the contract if …
they are somewhere on the internet
the customer is referred to them when the contract is concluded and can reasonably take note of them
the seller wants it
the customer signs, no matter what
Surprising clauses still do not become part of the contract.
What does not belong in a workshop order?
mileage
completion date
customer's religion
customer's signature
Only data needed for the order (data protection).
A manufacturer uses 12 AW per hour. A job is set at 18 AW. How long does it take?
1,0 hours
1,5 hours
1,8 hours
2,0 hours
When must a newly registered car go for its first main inspection?
after 12 months
after 24 months
after 36 months
after 48 months
After that every 24 months.
What minimum tread depth does the law require for car tyres?
1,0 mm
1,6 mm
3,0 mm
4,0 mm
More is recommended, about 4 mm for winter tyres.
A car's brake system usually works …
pneumatically
hydraulically
purely mechanically
electrically without fluid
Air brakes (pneumatic) are mainly found on trucks.
Why does brake fluid have to be changed regularly?
It evaporates
It absorbs water, the boiling point drops
It becomes thick
It attacks the paint
Vapour bubbles can reduce braking performance.
Which system prevents the wheels from locking when braking?
ESP
ABS
ASR
airbag
ESP prevents skidding, ASR prevents wheel spin.
Which vehicle document must be carried when driving?
registration certificate part II
registration certificate part I
CoC document
purchase contract
Part II is kept safely at home.
A customer collects his vehicle but does not pay the invoice. The workshop may …
sell the vehicle
keep the vehicle until payment
report the customer to the police
remove parts
Contractor's lien under § 647 BGB.
A non-binding cost estimate is clearly exceeded. What must the workshop do?
nothing
inform the customer beforehand
bear the extra costs itself
stop the repair
The customer can then cancel and only pays for the work so far.
After the statutory warranty has expired, a manufacturer voluntarily covers part of the repair costs. That is …
statutory warranty
guarantee
goodwill
product liability
Goodwill is voluntary and without legal entitlement.
The statutory warranty is claimed against …
the manufacturer
the seller
the insurance company
the inspection body
The guarantee is usually given by the manufacturer.
A customer does not return an old starter battery. The dealership charges …
nothing
a 7,50 € deposit
a 15 € disposal fee
double VAT
The deposit is refunded when the old battery is returned.
An end-of-life vehicle may only be handed in …
at any scrap dealer
at an approved dismantling company or collection point
abroad
at the recycling centre
The keeper receives a certificate of destruction.
The dealership wants to send advertising e-mails to workshop customers. This requires …
nothing, the address is known
the customer's consent
only an invoice
the manufacturer's approval
Advertising e-mails generally require consent. Exception: existing customers for similar offers, if they are told about their right to object (§ 7 (3) UWG).
What is reading the fault memory for?
for invoicing
to find faults in electronic systems
for registration
to change the mileage
Control units store faults that are read out via the CAN bus.
Which measure improves customer satisfaction after a workshop visit most directly?
raising prices
a follow-up call to check everything is fine
offering fewer appointments
sending the invoice later
Problems are spotted early and the customer feels valued.
A trainee is to assist a mechanic. What typically belongs to that?
carry out the diagnosis himself
provide parts from the warehouse and record working times
deregister vehicles
prepare expert reports
Commercial staff support the workshop organisationally.
Which stock key figure shows how often the stock is turned over in a year?
Storage period
Stock turnover rate
Storage interest rate
Reorder level
Stock turnover rate = cost of goods used / average stock.
Minimum stock 20 units, daily consumption 5 units, lead time 4 days. What is the reorder level?
20 units
40 units
25 units
100 units
Reorder level = 5 × 4 + 20 = 40 units.
What is the maximum stock level?
Minimum stock plus order quantity
Reorder level minus lead time
Minimum stock divided by consumption
Annual consumption
The maximum stock is the largest level that should be in stock after a delivery.
What is checked during goods receipt inspection?
Only the invoice amount
Compare quantity and condition with the delivery note and the order
Labour costs
Customer satisfaction
The goods are compared with the delivery note and the order, and deviations are reported.
A customer buys „ex works“. Who bears the transport risk?
The seller up to the customer
The buyer from the seller's works
The carrier alone
Nobody
With ex works, the risk passes to the buyer when the goods are made available at the seller's works.
A customer reports a defect. Which right takes priority?
Withdrawal from the contract
Price reduction
Subsequent performance
Damages
The buyer must first give the seller the chance to make subsequent performance.
Before winter, the parts store plans its demand for screen wash antifreeze. Which basis is most suitable?
Previous years' consumption, adjusted for current developments
The highest monthly consumption of last summer
The minimum order quantity of the cheapest supplier
The storage space that happens to be free right now
Demand planning is based on past figures and takes the season, vehicle base and trends into account.
Which term belongs to the EU tyre label?
Lifetime in kilometres
Wet grip
Price
Year of manufacture
The label shows fuel efficiency, wet grip and rolling noise.
What does ESP do?
It only prevents wheel lock under braking
It stabilises the vehicle when skidding through targeted braking
It controls steering
It switches the lights on
ESP intervenes when the vehicle is about to leave its course.
A supplier sells the same part it delivers to the vehicle manufacturer in its own packaging without the manufacturer's logo. What are such parts called?
Identical (OE supplier) parts
Replica (imitation) parts
Used parts
Remanufactured exchange parts
Identical parts come from the original equipment supplier and match the original part; replica parts are made by other manufacturers.
Autohaus Nordring GmbH concludes a training contract with a new trainee. Determine which arrangement for the probation period is permitted.
a probation period of two weeks so the trainee quickly has security
a probation period of three months
a probation period of six months, as usual for employees
no probation period at all if the trainee already did an internship in the company
a probation period of twelve months if the training period is shortened
§ 20 BBiG: the probation period must be at least one month and at most four months. It is compulsory, even after an internship.
During probation, trainee Sophie Kraus realises she does not like the occupation. Determine which statement about resigning is correct.
She can only resign with four weeks' notice and written reasons.
She can resign at any time without notice and without giving reasons; the notice must be in writing.
She can only resign with the prior consent of the IHK.
She can resign orally with two weeks' notice.
During probation only the training company can give notice.
§ 22 (1) and (3) BBiG: during probation both sides can give notice at any time without a notice period and without reasons, but only in writing.
The draft training contract of Autohaus Nordring GmbH contains the following agreements. Determine which agreement is void.
The probation period is three months.
The trainee keeps a record of training.
If the trainee drops out early, he pays a contractual penalty of 1.000 €.
Daily training time starts at 7:30.
The trainer provides training materials free of charge.
§ 12 (2) BBiG: contractual penalties are void. A record of training and free training materials are required by law (§§ 13, 14 BBiG).
Trainee Jonas Weber has a training contract until the end of summer. He passes the final exam a few weeks earlier. Determine when the training relationship ends.
at the end of the training period agreed in the contract
when the examination board announces the result
when the vocational school leaving certificate is handed over
at the end of the month in which the exam was passed
only when the written IHK certificate is received

§ 21 (2) BBiG: if the trainee passes before the end of the training period, the relationship ends when the examination board announces the result. If he continues working, a permanent employment relationship is deemed to exist (§ 24 BBiG).
Trainee Lara Klein has failed the final exam. Determine which statement is correct.
The training is automatically extended by exactly six months.
At her request the training relationship is extended until the next resit, by one year at most.
The training company alone decides whether the training is extended.
The training ends; a resit is only possible as an external candidate.
The exam cannot be retaken if one exam area was graded 'unsatisfactory'.
§ 21 (3) BBiG: at the trainee's request the relationship is extended until the next resit, by one year at most. The final exam can be retaken twice (§ 37 BBiG).

A new salesperson at Autohaus Nordring GmbH has agreed a six-month probation period in his contract; no collective agreement provides otherwise. Determine which statement about notice during probation is correct.
Both sides can give four weeks' notice to the 15th or end of a month.
Both sides can give two weeks' notice.
Both sides can give notice without any period, as in the probation period of training.
Only the employer can give notice; the employee is bound by the probation period.
General protection against dismissal already applies during probation, so a dismissal needs a reason.
§ 622 (3) BGB: in an agreed probation period of up to six months the notice period is two weeks, to any day. Protection under the KSchG only applies after six months.
Mr Doğan has worked in the workshop of Autohaus Nordring GmbH for one year and wants to resign; no collective agreement with different periods applies. Determine which statement is correct.
He must give one month's notice to the end of a month.
He can resign with four weeks' notice to the 15th or the end of a calendar month.
He can resign with two weeks' notice to any day.
He must observe the same extended period that applies to the employer based on his length of service.
Resignation by e-mail is also valid if the employer confirms receipt.

§ 622 (1) BGB: the basic notice period is four weeks (28 days) to the 15th or end of month; for employees it applies regardless of length of service. Notice must be in writing with a signature (§ 623 BGB).
Determine under which conditions an employee enjoys general protection against dismissal under the Dismissal Protection Act (KSchG).
from the first working day, regardless of company size
only after two years of service in companies with more than 20 employees
only in companies with a works council, regardless of length of service
if employment has lasted more than six months and the company regularly employs more than ten employees
only if the employee is over 50 or has a severe disability card
§§ 1, 23 KSchG: employment must have lasted more than six months and the company must regularly have more than ten employees. A dismissal then needs a personal, conduct-related or operational reason.
An employee of Autohaus Nordring GmbH considers his dismissal socially unjustified. Determine which statement about an action for protection against dismissal is correct.
He must file the action at the labour court within two weeks after his last working day.
He must file the action at the labour court within three weeks of receiving the written notice; otherwise the dismissal is deemed valid.
He must first file a complaint with the works council, which decides within a month.
He can file the action at the local court up to six months after employment ends.
He must file the action at the regional court within a month because it concerns his employment contract.
§§ 4, 7 KSchG: action at the labour court within three weeks of receiving the written notice, otherwise it is deemed valid from the start. The works council is not a court.
Autohaus Nordring GmbH dismisses an employee by e-mail. A PDF with the managing director's scanned signature is attached. Determine the legal position.
The dismissal is invalid because the statutory written form with a handwritten signature is missing.
The dismissal is valid as soon as the employee has opened the e-mail.
The dismissal is valid if the works council agreed beforehand.
The dismissal is valid because a scanned signature meets the written form.
The dismissal is valid but can be challenged by the employee within two weeks.
§ 623 BGB: notice of termination of employment requires written form with a handwritten signature; electronic form is excluded.
Trainee Ben turned 16 last autumn and will turn 17 in March. Use the extract to determine which statement about his statutory minimum holiday this calendar year is correct.
He gets 30 working days because he is not yet 17 at the start of the year.
He gets 27 working days because his age at the start of the calendar year is decisive.
He gets 25 working days because he turns 17 during the year.
He gets 27 working days pro rata until March and 25 pro rata after that.
He gets 24 working days like all employees under the Federal Holidays Act because he is a trainee.
§ 19 JArbSchG: the age at the start of the calendar year is decisive. Ben is then 16, i.e. not yet 17: at least 27 working days.

quiz: Determine which statement about the Working Hours Act for adult employees is correct.
After the end of daily working time an uninterrupted rest period of at least eleven hours must be observed.
Daily working time may regularly be twelve hours without compensation.
No break is required for working time over six hours if the employee agrees.
The rest period between two working days is at least twelve hours for adults and eleven hours for young people.
Sunday work is prohibited without exception, even for a workshop emergency service.
