An employee of Autohaus Nordring GmbH reports that she is pregnant. Determine which statement under the Maternity Protection Act is correct.
After the birth she may generally not be employed for eight weeks; in the last six weeks before the birth she may only work at her own express request.
In the last six weeks before the birth there is an absolute ban on employment, even if she wants to work.
She can shorten the protection period after the birth herself if she wants to return earlier.
The protection periods only apply to women in full-time employment.
The employer may give her ordinary notice with the statutory period during pregnancy.

§ 3 MuSchG: six weeks before the birth (work possible at her express request), generally eight weeks afterwards a ban on employment. § 17 MuSchG: no dismissal during pregnancy and until four months after the birth.
A salesperson at Autohaus Nordring GmbH has become a father and wants to take parental leave. Determine which statement is correct.
Only the mother can take parental leave; the father gets special leave instead.
Each parent is entitled to up to three years of parental leave per child; special protection against dismissal applies during it.
Parental leave totals at most 14 months for both parents together.
During parental leave the employer continues to pay full salary.
Parental leave must be taken in full before the child's third birthday and in one block.

§ 15 BEEG: up to three years per parent, up to 24 months of it between the third and eighth birthday. § 18 BEEG: protection against dismissal. Instead of salary there is parental allowance from the state; the 14 months concern the allowance.
Determine under which condition a works council can be elected in a company.
from at least ten employees, all of whom are of age
in companies with as a rule at least five permanent employees entitled to vote, three of whom are eligible for election
from 20 employees and only with the employer's consent
from at least three employees if a collective agreement applies
from 50 employees; in smaller companies the trade union represents the staff
§ 1 (1) BetrVG: as a rule at least five permanent employees entitled to vote, three of them eligible. The employer's consent is not required.
The management of Autohaus Nordring GmbH dismisses a warehouse employee without consulting the works council first. Determine the legal position.
The dismissal is invalid because the works council must be consulted before every dismissal.
The dismissal is valid, but the works council can challenge it within a week.
The dismissal is valid if there is a reason for dismissal.
The dismissal is only invalid if it was given during probation.
The dismissal is valid because the works council only has a right to information on dismissals.
§ 102 (1) BetrVG: the works council must be consulted before every dismissal; without consultation the dismissal is invalid. If it objects after consultation, the employer can still dismiss.
Determine in which matter the works council of Autohaus Nordring GmbH has a genuine right of co-determination.
buying land for a new branch
setting the selling prices for new cars
choosing the car brands the dealership represents
the start and end of daily working time including breaks
the amount of profit paid out to the shareholders

§ 87 (1) no. 2 BetrVG: the works council co-determines social matters such as working-time arrangements. Economic decisions are taken by the employer; there the works council at most has information and consultation rights.
A trainee at Autohaus Nordring GmbH is a member of the youth and trainee representation (JAV). Determine which statement about his being kept on after training is correct.
As a JAV member he is automatically kept on for a fixed two years.
If he requests continued employment in writing within the last three months before the end of training, a permanent employment relationship is deemed to exist.
He must first apply to the labour court to be kept on.
As a JAV member he has no special protection regarding being kept on.
He is kept on if a majority of trainees agree at a meeting.
§ 78a BetrVG: written request within the last three months. The employer can only escape this through the labour court if continued employment is unreasonable.
Determine which statement about collective agreements is correct.
A company collective agreement is concluded between a trade union and a single employer.
A company collective agreement is concluded between the works council and the employer.
Industry-wide agreements are concluded between an employers' association and the IHK.
Collective agreements are negotiated by the federal government with the unions.
Agreements between works council and employer always take priority over the collective agreement.

§ 2 TVG: the parties are trade unions and individual employers or employers' associations. Works council and employer conclude works agreements; these may generally not regulate pay set by collective agreement (§ 77 (3) BetrVG).
The industry-wide agreement binding Autohaus Nordring GmbH provides 30 days of holiday. A saleswoman's employment contract provides 32 days. Determine which statement is correct.
The employment contract applies because deviations from the collective agreement in the employee's favour are allowed (favourability principle).
The collective agreement applies because it always takes priority over the employment contract.
The statutory minimum holiday under the Federal Holidays Act applies because the two rules conflict.
The clause in the employment contract is void; the saleswoman must make up the extra days.
The average of both rules applies.
§ 4 (3) TVG (favourability principle): deviation from the collective agreement is allowed if it puts the employee in a better position. Worse terms would be invalid.
During ongoing collective bargaining in the motor trade, employees stop work for two hours. Determine which statement is correct.
It is a warning strike, allowed after the peace obligation has ended, to put pressure on the negotiations.
It is an indefinite strike that required a strike ballot with 75 % approval beforehand.
It is a lockout because work has stopped.
Work stoppages are always prohibited during ongoing negotiations.
It is a political strike, which is permitted in Germany.
Warning strikes are short stoppages during negotiations, allowed only after the peace obligation ends and without a ballot. A lockout is an employers' measure; political strikes are not permitted.
Determine which social security contribution or part of a contribution the employee pays alone.
the contribution to statutory accident insurance
the additional contribution to statutory health insurance
the contribution to unemployment insurance
the surcharge for childless persons in long-term care insurance
the insolvency benefit levy

The childless surcharge in long-term care insurance is paid by the employee alone (§ 58 SGB XI). The additional contribution and unemployment insurance are shared; accident insurance and the insolvency levy are paid by the employer alone.
A salesperson becomes unemployed after a branch closes. Determine which condition must be met for unemployment benefit (ALG I).
He must have been in insured employment for at least twelve months within the last 30 months and have registered as unemployed.
He must have paid pension contributions for at least five years.
He must prove that he has no assets of his own.
He must have resigned himself.
He must be over 25 and have completed vocational training.
§§ 137, 142, 143 SGB III: unemployment, registration and twelve months of insurance within a 30-month period. A means test applies to Bürgergeld; resigning oneself can lead to a blocking period.
The payroll department of Autohaus Nordring GmbH calculates an employee's total social security contribution. Determine to whom the amount is transferred.
to the tax office together with wage tax
to the employee's health insurance fund as collecting agency, which forwards the contributions to the other insurers
separately to each branch of insurance
to the Federal Employment Agency, which distributes the contributions
to the Berufsgenossenschaft because it is responsible for all employees

§ 28h SGB IV: the health insurance fund collects health, care, pension and unemployment contributions. Only the accident insurance contribution is paid by the employer directly to the Berufsgenossenschaft.
A supplier of Autohaus Nordring GmbH is a KG. Determine which statement about the limited partner (Kommanditist) of this KG is correct.
He manages the business and is liable without limit with his private assets.
He represents the KG alone externally and is liable only with his contribution.
He is excluded from management and is liable only up to the amount of his contribution.
He is liable without limit but excluded from management.
He first receives 4 % of his contribution; the rest of the profit is shared per head.

§§ 164, 170, 171 HGB: the limited partner is excluded from management and representation and is liable only up to his contribution. The general partner is liable without limit. All partners receive 4 % of profit; the rest is shared reasonably.
The manufacturer of the Nova brand is a public limited company (AG). Determine which statement about the bodies of an AG is correct.
The general meeting appoints the management board and supervises its management.
The supervisory board appoints the management board and supervises its management.
The management board elects the members of the supervisory board.
The works council appoints the management board if the company has more than 2.000 employees.
The register court appoints the management board on foundation for an unlimited period.

§§ 84, 111 AktG: the supervisory board appoints the management board (for at most five years) and supervises it. The general meeting elects the shareholder representatives on the supervisory board; in large companies employees elect their representatives.
An employee of Autohaus Nordring GmbH wants to become self-employed with a car valeting service and found a UG (haftungsbeschränkt). Determine which statement is correct.
The shareholders are additionally liable without limit with their private assets.
The share capital must be at least 25.000 €.
Each year the UG must put a quarter of its annual net profit into a statutory reserve.
The UG may employ at most ten people.
The UG is a partnership and is registered in section A of the commercial register.

§ 5a GmbHG: the UG is a form of GmbH with very low minimum capital (from 1 €). It must put 25 % of its annual net profit (less any loss carried forward) into a reserve. It is liable only with company assets and is registered in section B.

The management of Autohaus Nordring GmbH has internally forbidden Prokuristin Sabine Krüger to buy vehicles over 50.000,00 €. She nevertheless buys a used car for 60.000,00 €; the seller knows nothing of the ban. Determine the legal position.
The purchase contract is void because she exceeded her authority.
The purchase contract is provisionally ineffective until the management approves it.
The GmbH can rescind the contract for mistake.
The purchase contract is valid because a restriction of Prokura is ineffective towards third parties; internally she may be liable for damages.
The purchase contract is valid because by law holders of Prokura may only conclude transactions up to 100.000,00 € anyway.
§ 50 (1) HGB: restrictions on the scope of Prokura are ineffective towards third parties. Internally she may be liable for damages. There is no statutory amount limit.
Six-year-old Paul buys a comic for 3,50 € at a kiosk with his pocket money. Determine the legal position.
The purchase contract is void because Paul lacks legal capacity.
The purchase contract is valid under the pocket-money rule.
The purchase contract is provisionally ineffective until the parents approve it.
The purchase contract is valid because it is an everyday transaction.
The purchase contract is valid because Paul only gains a legal advantage.

§§ 104, 105 BGB: children under seven lack legal capacity; their declarations are void. § 110 BGB only applies to persons with limited capacity, the everyday-transactions rule (§ 105a BGB) only to adults without capacity.
A salesperson at Autohaus Nordring GmbH accidentally writes 18.900,00 € instead of 19.800,00 € in an offer for a used car. The customer accepts at once. Determine which option the GmbH has.
It can rescind the contract for fraudulent misrepresentation within one year.
It has no option because typing errors never justify rescission.
It can withdraw from the contract within 14 days without giving reasons.
It can rescind the contract for error in declaration without delay; it may have to compensate the customer's reliance loss.
It can rescind the contract for error in motive because it expected a higher profit.

§§ 119 (1), 121, 122 BGB: a slip of the pen is an error in declaration; rescission must be without delay and reliance loss must be compensated. An error in motive generally does not justify rescission; there was no fraud.
A workshop customer of Autohaus Nordring GmbH has not paid an invoice. Determine which statement about the regular limitation period of the claim is correct.
It is three years and starts at the end of the year in which the claim arose and the creditor became aware of it.
It is three years and starts on the day the invoice became due.
It is two years and starts when the repaired car is handed over.
It is thirty years because it is a money claim.
It is three years; afterwards the claim is extinguished, so a payment made anyway can be reclaimed.

§§ 195, 199 BGB: three years from the end of the year. Limitation only gives the debtor a right to refuse; whoever pays anyway cannot reclaim (§ 214 BGB). Two years apply to defect claims, 30 years e.g. to claims established by judgment.
A customer pays part of an open invoice of Autohaus Nordring GmbH as an instalment. Determine the effect on the limitation of the remaining claim.
Limitation is only suspended while the rest is being negotiated.
The limitation period is halved for the remaining amount.
Limitation is unchanged because only part was paid.
Limitation starts again because the customer acknowledged the claim by paying.
The remaining claim is immediately time-barred because the customer paid part of it.
§ 212 (1) no. 1 BGB: an acknowledgement, e.g. by a part payment, restarts the limitation period. Negotiations or legal action only suspend it.
Determine in which case a consumer has a statutory right of withdrawal.
She orders winter tyres in the online shop of Autohaus Nordring GmbH.
She buys a used car at the dealership after a test drive.
She buys a bicycle from a private person via a classified ads portal.
She buys a TV in an electronics store and wants to return it the next day.
She signs a repair order at the dealership's service desk.

§§ 312c, 312g, 355 BGB: right of withdrawal for distance and off-premises contracts between a business and a consumer. In a shop and between private persons there is no statutory right; exchanges there are goodwill.
A customer orders a child seat in the online shop of Autohaus Nordring GmbH and is properly informed of his right of withdrawal. Determine when the withdrawal period starts and how long it lasts.
It starts when the order is sent and lasts 14 days.
It starts as soon as the customer has received the goods and lasts 14 days.
It starts when the price is paid and lasts one month.
It starts when the goods are dispatched and lasts two weeks.
It starts on receipt of the goods and lasts 30 days because it is a safety product.

§§ 355, 356 (2) BGB: in consumer sales the 14-day period starts when the consumer has received the goods, and not before proper information. Without information the right expires at the latest after twelve months and 14 days.
Determine for which goods ordered in the online shop of Autohaus Nordring GmbH there is no statutory right of withdrawal.
floor mats from the standard range
seat covers embroidered with the customer's name to his specification
a roof rack in its original packaging
a child seat unpacked for inspection
a set of summer tyres already dispatched but not yet delivered
§ 312g (2) no. 1 BGB: no right of withdrawal for goods made to the customer's specification or clearly tailored to personal needs. Unpacking for inspection does not exclude withdrawal.
Households' disposable incomes rise significantly. Determine how this affects the new car market, all other conditions remaining the same.
The supply curve shifts to the right; the price falls.
The demand curve shifts to the left; the price falls.
The demand curve shifts to the right; equilibrium price and quantity rise.
The supply curve shifts to the left; the quantity rises.
There is only a movement along the demand curve; the curve itself stays the same.

For normal goods, demand rises at every price when income rises: the demand curve shifts to the right, and equilibrium price and quantity rise. A movement along the curve only occurs when the good's own price changes.
The price of fuel rises by 10 %; the quantity demanded falls by only 2 %. Determine how demand should be described.
elastic, because quantity reacts to the price rise
perfectly elastic, because even a small price change alters demand strongly
inelastic, because quantity reacts less strongly in percentage terms than price
perfectly inelastic, because quantity only falls slightly
abnormal, because quantity falls when the price rises

The change in quantity (2 %) is smaller than the change in price (10 %); price elasticity is below 1 in absolute terms. Demand would only be perfectly inelastic if quantity did not react at all. Falling quantity at a rising price is normal behaviour.
Determine how a supply monopolist differs from a seller in a polypoly on a perfect market.
He must accept the market price as given and can only adjust his quantity.
He can set price and sales quantity at will at the same time.
He is not supervised by the Federal Cartel Office.
He can set the price; how much he sells is then decided by the buyers.
He always makes the highest profit if he charges the highest possible price.

The monopolist is a price setter: he sets the price (or quantity) and buyers react. The polypolist is a quantity adjuster. Monopolies are subject to abuse control by the cartel office; the highest price does not automatically bring the highest profit.
Determine which description characterises the economic situation 'stagflation'.
strong growth with falling prices at the same time
falling prices with rising unemployment at the same time
weak or no growth with rising prices at the same time
stable prices with full employment at the same time
rising prices solely because of high demand in a boom
Stagflation = stagnation + inflation, e.g. after sharp rises in energy prices. Falling prices with rising unemployment mark deflation in a depression; demand-driven inflation marks a boom.
The figure shows the development of the consumer price index. Determine which statement is correct for the change from year 2 to year 3.
The inflation rate is 3,6 % because the index rose by 3,6 points.
The index rose by 3,6 points; this corresponds to an inflation rate of 3,0 %.
Prices have risen by 3,6 % since the base year.
The inflation rate is 23,6 % because the index is 23,6 points above the base year.
The purchasing power of money has risen because the index has risen.

Inflation rate = change in the index as a percentage of the previous year's value: (123,6 − 120,0) ÷ 120,0 × 100 = 3,0 %. Index points are not percent. Since the base year (100) prices have risen by 23,6 %. When the index rises, purchasing power falls.

f.cap: Consumer price index (base year = 100)

quiz: Due to the switch to electric cars, jobs at suppliers of combustion engines disappear permanently. Determine what type of unemployment this is and which measure best counters it.
seasonal unemployment – payment of seasonal short-time allowance
frictional unemployment – faster placement by the employment agency
structural unemployment – retraining and further training of those affected
cyclical unemployment – the ECB cutting key interest rates
structural unemployment – raising income tax to relieve the state budget
Structural unemployment results from lasting change in industries, technology or demand; it does not disappear with the next upswing. Qualification and retraining are most effective.
Determine which statement about classifying taxes is correct.
Wage tax is an indirect tax because the employer pays it over for the employee.
VAT is an indirect tax because the taxpayer (business) and the person bearing the tax (end consumer) are different.
Corporation tax is a consumption tax because it is levied on the profit of corporations.
Income tax is an indirect tax because it is paid in quarterly advance instalments.
Vehicle tax is a municipal tax and an indirect tax.

With indirect taxes the taxpayer and the person bearing the tax differ: the business pays VAT to the tax office, but the end consumer bears it economically. Wage, income, corporation and vehicle tax are direct taxes; vehicle tax goes to the federal government.
Determine who decides on key interest rates in the euro area in the ECB Governing Council.
the finance ministers of all EU member states
the heads of government of the euro countries together with the EU Commission
the boards of the large commercial banks in the euro area
the ECB Executive Board and the governors of the national central banks of the euro countries
the European Parliament on a proposal from the Deutsche Bundesbank
The Governing Council consists of the six members of the Executive Board and the governors of the national central banks of the euro countries. It is independent of governments and parliaments.

Autohaus Nordring GmbH bases its actions on the principle of sustainable development. Determine in which case a suitable measure is assigned to each of the three dimensions ecological – economic – social, in that order.
solar panels on the workshop roof – lower energy costs from own electricity – collectively agreed pay and health offers for staff
collectively agreed pay for staff – solar panels on the workshop roof – lower energy costs
lower energy costs – health offers for staff – solar panels on the workshop roof
more customer parking – higher advertising spend – cutting training places
solar panels on the workshop roof – cutting training places to save costs – lower energy costs

Three-pillar model: ecological (protect environment and resources), economic (be successful in the long term) and social (fair working conditions, responsibility for people). All three should be considered at the same time.
A customer wants his old vehicle scrapped. Determine which statement under the End-of-Life Vehicles Ordinance is correct.
He must hand the vehicle to a recognised collection or take-back point or a recognised dismantling company and receives a certificate of destruction.
He may give the vehicle to any scrap dealer; no certificate is needed.
He must send the vehicle back to the manufacturer at his own cost.
He may dismantle the vehicle himself and dispose of the remains with household waste.
A certificate of destruction is only needed if the vehicle is less than ten years old.
End-of-life vehicles may only be handed to recognised collection or take-back points or dismantling companies. The keeper presents the certificate of destruction when deregistering the vehicle.
To sign up for its newsletter, Autohaus Nordring GmbH asks for name, e-mail address, date of birth, income and religion. Determine which principle of the GDPR is mainly breached.
storage limitation
accuracy
right to data portability
data minimisation
integrity and confidentiality
Art. 5 (1) (c) GDPR: only data necessary for the purpose may be collected; an e-mail address is enough for a newsletter. Religion is also special category data (Art. 9 GDPR).
A customer asks Autohaus Nordring GmbH which personal data it stores about him. Determine which statement is correct.
The dealership must reply within 72 hours and may charge a fee.
The dealership must reply without delay, at the latest within one month; the first copy of the data is free.
The dealership only has to reply if the customer gives a legitimate reason.
The dealership has a year because the data must be compiled from different systems.
The dealership may refuse while the customer still has unpaid invoices.
Art. 12 (3) and Art. 15 GDPR: information without delay, within one month at the latest (extendable in exceptional cases). The first copy is free; the customer need not give a reason.
A laptop with unencrypted customer data is stolen from a salesperson's car. Determine what Autohaus Nordring GmbH must generally do under the GDPR.
Report the incident to the police within 14 days, but not to the data protection authority.
Report the incident to the competent data protection authority, if possible within 72 hours of becoming aware of it.
Act only if affected customers complain.
Report the incident to the IHK within one month.
No report is needed because the laptop was stolen and not passed on deliberately.
Art. 33 GDPR: report to the supervisory authority without delay and if possible within 72 hours, unless there is probably no risk. If the risk is high, those affected must also be notified (Art. 34).

Health and safety measures in the workshop of Autohaus Nordring GmbH are to be reviewed. Determine who is responsible for the risk assessment of workplaces under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.
the works council, because it represents the employees' interests
the employer, even if advised by occupational safety specialists
the Berufsgenossenschaft, which inspects every company annually
each employee for his own workplace
the trade supervisory office, which prepares the assessment on the company's behalf
§§ 3, 5 ArbSchG: the employer must identify hazards and set protective measures. He may be advised by safety specialists and company doctors but remains responsible.
A round blue sign with a white ear protection symbol hangs in the workshop of Autohaus Nordring GmbH. Determine which statement is correct.
It is a prohibition sign: ear protection may not be worn here.
It is a mandatory sign: ear protection must be worn here.
It is a warning sign: it warns of noise; ear protection is optional.
It is an emergency sign: ear protection for emergencies is kept here.
It is a fire protection sign: it marks a fire alarm.
ASR A1.3: blue and round = mandatory, round with red rim and bar = prohibition, yellow triangle = warning, green rectangle = emergency and first aid, red square = fire protection.
A sole trader's equity is €380,000 at the start of the year and €420,000 at the end. During the year he withdrew €30,000 and contributed €10,000. What is the profit?
Profit = closing equity − opening equity + withdrawals − contributions = 420,000 − 380,000 + 30,000 − 10,000 = €60,000.

Account 1400 Receivables shows: opening balance €48,000, increases €210,000, decreases €195,000. What is the closing balance and on which side of account 1400 is it entered when the account is closed?
€63,000 on the credit side
€63,000 on the debit side
€33,000 on the credit side
€453,000 on the debit side

Asset account: opening balance + increases − decreases = €63,000. The account has a debit balance. The closing balance is entered on the smaller side to balance it, i.e. the credit side of account 1400 (contra entry on the debit side of the closing balance account).
At year end, total income is €1,910,000 and total expenses are €1,840,000. Which closing entry is correct?
Equity to Profit and loss account €70,000
Profit and loss account to Closing balance account €70,000
Profit and loss account to Equity €3,750,000
Profit and loss account to Equity €70,000
Income exceeds expenses, so the profit is €70,000. The balance is on the debit side of the P&L account and increases equity on the credit side.
In the advance return period, output VAT is €4,200 and input VAT is €5,100. What is the result?
A VAT payable of €900
An input VAT surplus of €900, i.e. a claim against the tax office
A VAT payable of €9,300
No effect, because the amounts cancel out
If input VAT exceeds output VAT, the company is entitled to a refund: 5,100 − 4,200 = €900.
A customer receives an invoice on credit for €30,000 net plus 19% VAT. What is the journal entry (1400 receivables, 8000 revenue, 1770 output VAT, 1570 input VAT)?
8000 Revenue new cars €30,000 and 1770 Output VAT €5,700 to 1400 Trade receivables €35,700
1400 Trade receivables €35,700 to 8000 Revenue new cars €35,700
1400 Trade receivables €30,000 and 1570 Deductible input VAT €5,700 to 8000 Revenue new cars €35,700
1400 Trade receivables €35,700 to 8000 Revenue new cars €30,000 and 1770 Output VAT €5,700
Receivables increase on the debit side by the gross amount; revenue (net) and output VAT (30,000 × 19% = €5,700) are credited.

A vehicle lift has a list price of €25,000 net. The supplier grants a 4% discount, and 2% cash discount is deducted on payment. Freight and installation cost €1,200 net. Useful life 8 years, acquired in April. What is the straight-line depreciation in the first year?

A tow truck (acquisition cost €50,000, useful life 10 years) is acquired in January 2026 and depreciated on a declining-balance basis at the highest permitted rate. What is the depreciation in year 2?

For acquisitions from July 2025 to December 2027, the rate is at most three times the straight-line rate and no more than 30%. Year 1: €15,000; year 2: 30% of the remaining book value of €35,000 = €10,500.
A dealership's operationally necessary capital is €800,000 and the imputed interest rate is 6%. How much is the imputed interest per year?
Imputed interest = operationally necessary capital × interest rate = 800,000 × 6% = €48,000. It also covers interest on equity.

In the cost allocation sheet, €60,000 of costs from the service cost centre Administration are allocated by headcount: new cars 4, used cars 2, parts and accessories 3, workshop 11. How much does the workshop receive?
€60,000 / 20 employees = €3,000 per employee, × 11 = €33,000.

According to the cost allocation sheet, the workshop has €540,000 of overheads and €300,000 of productive wages. A job takes 4 hours at €30 productive wage per hour, and the profit mark-up is 10%. What is the net price for the labour?
Overhead rate = 540,000 / 300,000 = 180%. Wages €120 + €216 overheads = €336 total cost + 10% profit = €369.60.

Forward calculation for a roof box: list purchase price €400, supplier discount 20%, supplier cash discount 2%, delivery costs €12, overhead mark-up 30%, profit 10%, customer cash discount 2%, no customer discount. What is the net selling price on credit terms?

Net purchase price 320 → cash purchase price 313.60 → landed cost 325.60 → total cost 423.28 → cash selling price 465.61. Customer cash discount is calculated on the higher price: 465.61 / 0.98 = €475.11.

Backward calculation: a set of rims is to be offered for €500 net (list selling price). Customer discount 10%, customer cash discount 2%, profit 5%, overhead mark-up 25%. What is the maximum landed cost that can be paid?
500 − 10% = 450 − 2% = €441 cash selling price. Profit and overheads were added as mark-ups, so divide: 441 / 1.05 = 420 / 1.25 = €336.

Margin calculation: a set of complete wheels has a landed cost of €2,400, and the overhead mark-up is 35%. The market price is at most €3,300 net (no discounts). What is the profit as a percentage of total cost?
An accessory item is priced with a mark-up of 25% on landed cost. What is the gross margin (as a percentage of the selling price)?
The mark-up refers to the landed cost (100 → 125), the margin to the selling price: 25 / 125 × 100 = 20%.
A fleet customer offers 30 services at €180 net each. Variable costs are €140 and full costs €210 per service. The workshop has spare capacity. What should be decided?
Reject: there is a loss of €900
Accept: the operating result improves by €1,200
Accept: the operating result improves by €5,400
Reject: the price is below variable costs
Fixed costs are incurred anyway. The contribution margin decides: (180 − 140) × 30 = €1,200 extra.
A car wash has fixed costs of €36,000 a year. One wash earns €12 net, and the variable cost per wash is €3. At how many washes does it break even?
3,000 washes
2,400 washes
4,000 washes
12,000 washes
Break-even quantity = fixed costs / unit contribution margin = 36,000 / (12 − 3) = 4,000 washes.
Cash and cash equivalents €60,000, receivables €140,000, inventories €520,000, current liabilities €250,000. What is the quick ratio (2nd-degree liquidity)?
(Cash + receivables) / current liabilities × 100 = 200,000 / 250,000 × 100 = 80%. Inventories only count for 3rd-degree liquidity.
A dealership has €600,000 equity and €1,800,000 debt. What is the equity ratio?
Equity ratio = equity / total capital × 100 = 600,000 / 2,400,000 × 100 = 25%.
Profit €90,000, interest on debt €54,000, equity €600,000, debt €1,800,000. What is the return on total capital?
(Profit + interest on debt) / total capital × 100 = 144,000 / 2,400,000 × 100 = 6%.
Parts warehouse: opening stock €180,000, closing stock €220,000, cost of goods sold for the year €1,200,000. What is the average storage period (360 days)?
6 days
60 days
54 days
66 days
Average stock = (180,000 + 220,000) / 2 = €200,000. Turnover rate = 1,200,000 / 200,000 = 6; storage period = 360 / 6 = 60 days.
Target headcount 42, current headcount 38. Confirmed leavers: 3 (retirement and resignations). Confirmed joiners: 2 apprentices taken on. What is the net staffing requirement?
Net requirement = target − (current + joiners − leavers) = 42 − (38 + 2 − 3) = 5.
Which selection method puts several candidates through different exercises at the same time, such as role play, presentation and group discussion, assessed by several observers?
Structured job interview
Assessment centre
Personnel questionnaire
Work sample
An assessment centre uses several exercises and observers to test mainly social and methodological skills, e.g. for sales or service reception roles.

A service employee earns a gross salary of €3,200, including €40 employer savings contribution. Tax deductions are €410 and the employee's social security contribution is €680. The €40 savings instalment is transferred directly to the building society. What is the payout amount?
Net = 3,200 − 410 − 680 = €2,110. The savings instalment goes to the building society: 2,110 − 40 = €2,070.
The workshop has total annual costs of €1,080,000 and sells 12,000 hours. The profit mark-up is 8%. What is the net hourly labour rate?
Cost per hour sold = 1,080,000 / 12,000 = €90, plus 8% profit = €97.20.
A mechanics team is present for 1,600 hours in a month, of which 1,360 hours are clocked on customer jobs; 1,496 hours are invoiced. Which statement is correct?
Utilisation 110%, efficiency 85%
Utilisation 85%, efficiency 90.9%
Utilisation 85%, efficiency 110%
Utilisation 117.6%, efficiency 110%
Utilisation = clocked / attendance hours = 1,360 / 1,600 = 85%. Efficiency = invoiced / clocked hours = 1,496 / 1,360 = 110% (overall productivity: 1,496 / 1,600 = 93.5%).
From the dealership's point of view, what is an advantage of ordering new cars mainly against specific customer orders rather than for stock?
The customer receives the car faster
More cars are available for spontaneous test drives
No capital is tied up in unsold cars and there is no sales risk
The manufacturer generally pays higher stock bonuses for it
A car ordered for a customer is already sold. Stock cars tie up capital, cause holding costs and still have to find a buyer.
A manufacturer-owned branch (Werksniederlassung) is …
a sales outlet owned by the manufacturer that sells directly to end customers
an independent dealer with contractually guaranteed territorial protection
an authorised workshop that does not sell new cars
a wholesaler that passes vehicles on only to sub-dealers
Branches belong to the manufacturer's group and are part of direct distribution. The manufacturer bears the costs and risks itself.
Which question is an open question in the needs analysis?
Would you like a diesel again?
Would you like the car in white or in black?
Have you already had a test drive?
What will you mainly use the car for?
Open questions (W-questions) let the customer answer freely and reveal needs and buying motives. The others are closed questions or an either-or question.

According to the contract, a new car is to be delivered to a consumer two months after the contract is concluded. Before delivery, the manufacturer raises its list prices. May the dealership charge more on the basis of a price adjustment clause in its general terms and conditions?
Yes, if the manufacturer provides written proof of the increase
No, a clause allowing price increases for delivery within four months is invalid against consumers
Yes, but by no more than the inflation rate
Only if the customer finances the purchase price
Under § 309 No. 1 BGB, standard-term clauses providing for a price increase on goods to be delivered within four months of conclusion of the contract are invalid.
What does the eVB number prove at registration?
that comprehensive insurance has been taken out
that motor third-party liability insurance is in place
that the vehicle tax has been paid in advance
the EU type approval of the vehicle
The electronic insurance confirmation (eVB) is issued by the liability insurer. No vehicle can be registered without proof of compulsory insurance.
What does the EU certificate of conformity (CoC) certify?
that the buyer owns the vehicle
that the vehicle has passed its roadworthiness test
that the purchase price has been paid in full
that the vehicle conforms to an approved EU vehicle type
With the CoC the manufacturer confirms that the vehicle conforms to its EU type approval. It is the basis for first registration.
Which document must be carried when driving and shown on request?
Registration certificate part I
Registration certificate part II
EU certificate of conformity (CoC)
Purchase contract

Part I (vehicle registration document) must be carried under the vehicle registration regulation. Part II (vehicle title) should not be kept in the car because it is needed for sale and change of keeper.
When buying a new car, a customer wants to trade in a vehicle that is still financed. What must the dealership pay particular attention to?
A trade-in is legally impossible
The customer must first sell the vehicle privately
The outstanding loan must be paid off so that the dealership obtains ownership and registration certificate part II
The dealership automatically takes over the customer's loan agreement
The bank is usually the owner by way of security and holds part II. The dealership asks for the settlement amount, pays it off and offsets it against the trade-in price.
Why is professional reconditioning of used cars before sale worthwhile?
It extends the statutory liability for defects
It replaces the roadworthiness test
It makes defect disclosures in the contract unnecessary
It improves the first impression, shortens the holding period and raises the achievable price
A well-presented car looks more valuable, sells faster and thus reduces holding costs. Reconditioning does not change any legal obligations.
A dealership buys a car from a private individual for €10,000 and sells it under the margin scheme for €11,900. How much is the VAT?
Only the margin of €1,900 is taxed, and it is a gross amount: €1,900 × 19/119 = €303.36 (§ 25a UStG).
A dealership wants to shorten the limitation period for defect claims to one year when selling a used car to a consumer. What has been required for this since 2022?
The consumer must be specifically informed before the contract is concluded and the reduction must be agreed expressly and separately
A note in the terms and conditions on the back of the contract is sufficient
A reduction is never permitted with consumers
The buyer must also take out warranty insurance
This is laid down in § 476(2) BGB. Without the separate notice, the statutory period of two years applies.
A dealership buys several used cars from another dealership (commercial transaction on both sides). What must it do after delivery to preserve its rights regarding defects?
Nothing, liability for defects lasts two years anyway
Report defects at the latest before one year has passed
Inspect the vehicles without undue delay and give notice of any defects found without undue delay
Withdraw from the contract within 14 days
Between merchants, the duty to inspect and give notice under § 377 HGB applies. Anyone who does not give notice in time loses the rights for these defects because the goods are deemed accepted.
After the liability for defects and the manufacturer's warranty have expired, the manufacturer voluntarily pays half the cost of an engine failure. This is …
goodwill
a warranty service
liability for defects
product liability
Goodwill is a voluntary gesture with no legal entitlement. It serves customer loyalty and the brand image.
What applies when a financed vehicle is transferred by way of security (Sicherungsübereignung)?
The customer remains owner, the bank becomes direct possessor
The bank receives registration certificate part I
The bank becomes owner, the customer remains possessor and may use the vehicle
The vehicle is parked at the bank until the last instalment
The bank becomes owner by way of security and keeps part II, while the customer continues to use the car. After full repayment, ownership and part II return to the customer.
Which interest rate includes, in addition to the borrowing rate, other credit costs such as processing fees and is therefore suitable for comparing finance offers?
the borrowing (nominal) rate
the base rate
the default interest rate
the annual percentage rate (APR)
The APR expresses the total cost of credit as an annual percentage. It must be stated to consumers under the Price Indication Ordinance.
A consumer signs a loan agreement to finance a car at the dealership and is properly informed of the right of withdrawal. Can the consumer withdraw from the loan agreement?
No, because the contract was concluded on the business premises
Yes, within 14 days
Yes, within 7 days
Yes, within one month after handover of the vehicle

Consumer loans can be withdrawn from within 14 days regardless of where they were concluded (§§ 495, 355 BGB). With a linked purchase contract, the customer is then no longer bound by it either (§ 358 BGB).
Compared with an instalment loan without a final balloon payment, the same term and the same interest rate, what is a typical disadvantage of balloon financing for the customer?
higher monthly instalments
higher total interest costs because the balloon payment bears interest over the whole term
no right of withdrawal
the vehicle may not be registered
The balloon payment is only repaid at the end, so the outstanding balance stays high for longer. Monthly instalments are lower, but total interest is higher.
Under a residual value lease, the lessor sells the returned vehicle for less than the agreed residual value. Who bears the difference?
the lessee
the lessor
the arranging dealership
the manufacturer
In residual value leasing, the lessee bears the residual value risk and must make up a shortfall. Depending on the contract, any surplus is credited to the lessee in full or in part.
With otherwise identical terms, what is the effect of a higher initial lease payment (down payment)?
The calculated residual value rises
The term is extended
The lessee becomes owner at the end of the contract
The monthly lease instalments fall
The initial payment is an advance payment spread over the term. It lowers the instalments but strains liquidity at the start.
A customer who only has motor third-party liability insurance causes a rear-end collision. What does the insurer cover?
the damage to both vehicles
only the damage to the customer's own vehicle
the other party's damage, but not the damage to the customer's own vehicle
nothing, because the customer caused the accident
Liability insurance covers damage caused to third parties. Only comprehensive cover pays for damage to one's own vehicle.
A customer has an at-fault accident claim settled through comprehensive cover and has no no-claims protection. What usually happens?
Nothing, comprehensive claims do not affect the no-claims class
The policy ends automatically
The no-claims class is downgraded and the premium rises
Only the partial cover premium becomes more expensive
A settled comprehensive claim leads to a downgrade to a worse no-claims class the following year. For small claims, paying oneself can be cheaper.
An unknown person deliberately scratches the paint of a parked car. Under the usual model conditions (AKB), which insurance pays for the damage?
motor third-party liability
partial cover (Teilkasko)
the breakdown/assistance cover
comprehensive cover (Vollkasko)
Malicious damage by third parties (vandalism) is a comprehensive-cover claim. Partial cover includes theft, glass breakage, storm and collisions with game, among others.
A leased car is stolen. The comprehensive insurer pays the replacement value, but the lessor demands a higher settlement amount. What covers this gap?
GAP insurance
motor third-party liability
the breakdown/assistance cover
payment protection insurance

GAP cover pays the difference between the replacement value and the lease settlement or outstanding loan. Payment protection insurance, by contrast, applies e.g. in case of death or incapacity to work.
Which service is typically part of a motor assistance cover (Schutzbrief)?
Compensation for damage the driver causes to others
Roadside assistance and towing of the vehicle
Repair of at-fault accident damage
Refund of the purchase price after theft
Assistance cover provides help on the road such as breakdown service, towing, vehicle return or overnight costs. It does not cover damage to the vehicle itself.
Which CRM measure at a dealership mainly serves to retain existing customers?
timely contact before roadworthiness test, service and contract end dates based on customer data
buying third-party address lists for sales calls
discount campaigns only for new customers
deleting all customer data right after vehicle handover
CRM uses stored customer data to make suitable offers at the right time. Marketing contacts require the consent needed under data protection and competition law.
List price €200, 10% trade discount, 2% cash discount, delivery costs €6. What is the landed purchase price?
€200 − €20 discount = €180; − €3.60 cash discount = €176.40; + €6 delivery costs = €182.40.
Weighted scoring table: supplier A scores 5 points for quality (weight 40%) and 3 points for price (weight 60%). What is its weighted score?
4.0 points
4.2 points
3.8 points
3.4 points
Maximum stock 150 units, minimum stock 30 units. The delivery arrives exactly when the minimum stock is reached. What is the order quantity?
90 units
180 units
120 units
150 units
Order quantity = maximum stock − minimum stock = 150 − 30 = 120 units.
Commercial sale between two merchants: a material defect in brake pads, not detectable at goods-in inspection, appears after two months. What must the dealership do?
Nothing, the notification period has already expired
Notify the supplier without undue delay after discovery
Notify only once a customer complains about the defect
Notify the supplier within six months of discovery
Under § 377(3) HGB, hidden defects must be reported without undue delay after discovery; otherwise the goods are deemed accepted.
A dealership with three branches keeps all spare parts at one site and supplies the branches from there. This is a …
flow-through warehouse
central warehouse
third-party warehouse
decentralised warehouse
Central storage reduces stock and tied-up capital but lengthens the routes to the branches.
A parts store has an inventory turnover rate of 8. What is the average storage period?
80 days
36 days
8 days
45 days
Average storage period = 360 ÷ turnover rate = 360 ÷ 8 = 45 days.
Each item is counted once during the financial year; the stock on the balance sheet date comes from the continuous stock records. This is …
perpetual inventory
year-end stocktaking
shifted-date inventory
sample-based inventory
Perpetual inventory requires reliable stock records that capture all receipts and issues.
The dealership orders in response to a binding offer but demands an extra 5% discount in the order. Legally, the order is …
a new offer to the supplier
an order confirmation
a valid acceptance of the offer
a non-binding enquiry
An acceptance with changes counts as a rejection combined with a new offer (§ 150(2) BGB).
A supplier is late delivering ordered rims. The dealership wants to withdraw from the contract and buy elsewhere. What is normally required first?
Agree on a contractual penalty
Report the supplier to the chamber of commerce
Start court dunning proceedings
Set a reasonable additional deadline
Withdrawal and damages in lieu of performance generally require a reasonable additional deadline to have expired without result (§§ 323, 281 BGB).
A private customer complains to the dealership about a new alternator eight months after purchase. What is the burden of proof?
After six months there are no warranty rights left
The defect is presumed to have existed at handover
The manufacturer must prove the cause to the customer
The customer must prove the defect existed at handover
In consumer sales, for one year after handover the defect is presumed to have existed at handover (§ 477 BGB); the dealer would have to prove otherwise.
A business customer receives a workshop invoice with no agreed payment date. When, at the latest, is he in default without a reminder?
Immediately on receipt of the invoice
30 days after due date and receipt of the invoice
14 days after the invoice date
Only after the third reminder
This is set out in § 286(3) BGB; for consumers the 30-day rule only applies if the invoice points out this consequence.
A customer buys a roof box with base carrier. What should the salesperson definitely point out?
Observe the permitted roof load including carrier and box
The roof box must be entered in the vehicle documents
With a roof box, driving is only allowed in daylight
With a roof box, load securing is no longer required
The permitted roof load is stated in the owner's manual; carrier, box and contents together must not exceed it.
"Yes, these brake pads cost a bit more, but they last much longer." Which objection-handling method is this?
Yes-but method
Boomerang method
Pre-emption method
Counter-question method
The salesperson first agrees with the objection and then counters it with a benefit argument.
A customer wants to return defect-free, unopened wiper blades bought in the shop because he does not like them. What is the legal position?
He has a right to subsequent performance
He has a statutory 14-day right of withdrawal
No legal right; an exchange is a goodwill gesture
He has a right to a price reduction
A right of withdrawal only exists for distance and off-premises contracts; without a defect there are no warranty rights.
Does a workshop customer have to pay for a cost estimate?
Only if the estimate is non-binding
Always, because it takes working time
Only if the workshop is a master-craft business
Only if this was agreed beforehand
Under § 632(3) BGB, a cost estimate is not to be paid for unless otherwise agreed.
Why are brake pads always replaced per axle?
Because otherwise the brake fluid overheats
So that left and right brake equally hard
Because the periodic inspection requires it
So that the ABS does not need to be re-learned
Unevenly worn pads on one axle cause unequal braking, so the vehicle may pull to one side.
Since 1 October 2024, which tyres meet the winter tyre requirement in wintry road conditions?
All tyres with at least 4 mm tread depth
All tyres marked M+S
Only tyres with the Alpine symbol (mountain with snowflake)
All all-season tyres regardless of marking
The transition period for tyres marked only M+S expired on 30 September 2024.
The windscreen of a vehicle with a front camera has been replaced. Which work step is required afterwards?
Re-programming all of the vehicle's radio keys
Calibrating the front camera to manufacturer specifications
Entering the windscreen in the registration certificate
Changing the brake fluid to manufacturer specifications
Camera-based assistance systems such as lane keeping or emergency braking only work reliably with a correctly aligned camera.
Who may de-energise the high-voltage system of an electric vehicle?
Any apprentice from the second year onwards
A specialist qualified for high-voltage systems
Any employee after a short verbal briefing
The service advisor at vehicle reception
Work on the HV system requires special qualification under German accident-insurance (DGUV) rules; staff who are only made aware may carry out non-electrical work only.
What does a flexible service interval (longlife service) mean?
Oil changes are no longer needed for the vehicle's whole life
The inspection is done yearly regardless of mileage
The vehicle calculates the date from driving style and oil condition
The customer sets the date entirely as he likes
Sensors and software evaluate usage and operating conditions; an approved longlife oil is usually required.
Significant defects are found during the periodic technical inspection (HU). What follows?
Only a note in the report; the sticker is issued anyway
Vehicle is taken off the road immediately and must be towed
Sticker is issued; repair the defects by the next inspection
No sticker; repair the defects and have them re-checked within one month
The sticker is only issued after a successful re-inspection; if the one-month deadline is missed, a complete new inspection is required.
After an accident, liability is split 70:30 against the other party. What does the other party's liability insurer pay the customer?
100% of the damage
30% of the damage
50% of the damage
70% of the damage
Compensation follows the liability ratio; the customer bears the rest himself or via his comprehensive (fully comp) cover.
Which damage to one's own vehicle is typically covered by partial casco insurance?
A rear-end collision caused by oneself
Hail damage to roof and bonnet
Paint scratched by vandalism
A bollard scraped while manoeuvring
Partial casco covers fire, theft, glass breakage, storm, hail and collisions with game, among others; vandalism and self-caused accidents fall under fully comprehensive cover.
For a minor third-party liability claim, what is usually sufficient to quantify the damage?
A cost estimate from the workshop
A report by an independent appraiser
A verbal estimate by the customer
A damage estimate by the police
For minor damage, appraiser fees are considered disproportionate and are often not reimbursed; a cost estimate is enough.
The injured party in a liability claim rents an equivalent replacement vehicle. What is often deducted?
The deductible of his own comprehensive cover
Vehicle tax for the rental period
The cost of the damage report
Saved running costs of his own vehicle
Because his own car is not being worn during this time, a share for saved own costs is deducted; renting one class lower usually avoids this.
An injured party has a second car he can use without restriction and claims compensation for loss of use. As a rule …
There is no claim, as there is no noticeable loss of use
He gets double the daily rate because of two vehicles
He gets loss-of-use compensation and a rental car at once
His own casco insurer pays the loss-of-use compensation
Loss-of-use compensation requires the will and the possibility to use the car; an available second car usually rules out a noticeable impairment.
What is the purpose of a light-liquid (oil) separator in the workshop or at the wash bay?
It separates used oil from brake fluid for reuse
It filters brake dust from the air in the workshop
It keeps oil and fuel out of the waste water
It cleans exhaust gases during the emissions test
Light liquids must not enter the sewer system; the separator must be serviced and emptied regularly.
A round blue safety sign with a white symbol, e.g. safety goggles, is a …
emergency/escape sign
warning sign
prohibition sign
mandatory sign
Blue means mandatory action, red means prohibition or fire protection, yellow means warning and green means rescue/escape.
What typically belongs in a job posting but not in the job description?
Authority and deputy arrangements of the position
How to apply and the desired start date
Position of the job in the hierarchy
Goals and tasks of the position
The job description is an internal document about the position itself. How to apply and the start date are only needed in the posting, which addresses applicants.

lf: LF 2 · Commercial management and control
Stocktaking and inventory
Stocktaking = counting and valuing, inventory = the list that results.
Physical stocktaking (counting) and book stocktaking (documents).
Methods: reporting date (±10 days), shifted (3 months before, 2 months after), permanent.
Occasions: founding, end of the financial year, dissolution.
Lower of cost or market: the lower value counts.
Inventory: assets (by liquidity), debts (by due date), net worth = assets − debts.
Balance sheet
Assets: fixed and current assets. Liabilities: equity and debt. Totals always equal.
Ratios: equity ratio, debt ratio, fixed asset coverage I and II.
Asset exchange and liability exchange: total stays. Increase and decrease on both sides: total rises or falls.
Accounts and closing
Asset account: opening balance and increases on the debit side. Liability account: on the credit side.
Journal = chronological (booking records), ledger = by subject (T-accounts).
Balance sheet accounts → closing balance sheet. Income statement accounts → P&L → equity.
Affects profit if an expense or income account is involved.
Every sale: revenue booking + VAK booking. Revenue − VAK = gross profit.
Operating result + neutral result = profit or loss.
VAT
19 % standard rate, 7 % reduced; insurance, interest, residential rent tax-exempt.
Value added tax: the value added at each stage is taxed, it is borne by the end consumer.
Transitory item: no expense, no income.
VAT payable = output VAT − input VAT; advance return usually monthly.
Closing: 1770 to 1570, VAT payable 1770 to 1200.
LF 9 · Personnel
Planning and recruitment
Quantitative (how many) and qualitative (which qualification). Replacement, new, reduced demand.
Requirement = target − (current + arrivals − departures).
Internal: fast, cheap, motivating. External: new ideas, wider choice.
Inadmissible questions: pregnancy, religion, party, trade union.
Employment contract: parties, start, job, place, pay, working hours, leave, probation, notice periods.
Collective agreements and protective laws
Free collective bargaining, peace obligation. Framework agreement (conditions) and pay agreement (money).
Process: negotiation, arbitration, strike ballot 75 %, strike, agreement, ballot 25 %.
Working hours: 8 hours, max. 10; break 30/45 minutes; rest period 11 hours.
Maternity protection: 6 weeks before, 8 weeks after birth; ban on dismissal.
Leave: 24 working days, full after 6 months, otherwise 1/12 per month.
Salary and taxes
Gross (+ taxable benefit) − income tax − solidarity surcharge − church tax − social insurance = net − private deductions = payout.
Social insurance split half and half: health 14,6 % + additional, care 3,6 %, pension 18,6 %, unemployment 2,6 %; accident employer only.
Company car: 1 % of gross list price + 0,03 % per km of commute distance.
Taxable income: income − income-related expenses − special expenses − extraordinary burdens.
Private provision: occupational disability, liability, „Riester“, company pension.
Termination
Dismissal, termination agreement, expiry of term, retirement. Always in writing.
Ordinary with notice; extraordinary for good cause within 2 weeks.
Reasons: personal, conduct-related (warning), operational (social selection).
Special protection: pregnant women, works council, severely disabled, apprentices.
Consult the works council; lawsuit within 3 weeks; reference simple or qualified.
LF 10 · Managing value creation
Cost and performance accounting
Stages: cost types, cost centres (BAB), cost units (pricing).
Expense ≠ cost: neutral (non-operational, other periods, extraordinary), basic, different, additional costs.
Direct costs directly, overheads via keys. Main cost centres: new cars, used cars, parts, workshop.
Overhead rate = overheads / direct costs × 100.
Pricing forward, backward, difference; markup, factor, trade margin.
Contribution margin and workshop
CM = revenue − variable costs; operating result = CM − fixed costs.
Short-term price floor = variable costs. Break-even = fixed costs / unit CM.
Multi-level: CM 1 (gross profit), CM 2, CM 3, operating result.

Hourly labour rate = average wage × workshop index. Target index = target labour revenue / productive wages, with profit and risk both calculated on cost. Actual index = actual labour revenue / productive wages.
Controlling
Structured balance sheet: fixed and current assets on the assets side, equity and debt (long- and short-term) on the liabilities side. The ratios are formed from these.

Financing (liabilities side): equity ratio and debt-to-equity show independence and creditworthiness. Dealerships often have low ratios because of financed vehicles, so always compare with the previous year or the industry.
Investment (assets side): fixed asset intensity shows how much is tied up long term. High intensity means high fixed costs and little flexibility.
Golden balance sheet rule: finance fixed assets long term. Fixed asset coverage II at least 100 %, otherwise refinance or strengthen equity.

Liquidity levels 1 to 3: can the dealership pay its short-term debts? Rule of thumb: level 2 ≥ 100 %, level 3 clearly above. At a dealership the money is in the vehicles, short days in stock are decisive.

Returns: equity (profit / equity), total capital ((profit + interest) / total capital), sales (profit / revenue), each × 100. Assess: compare return on equity with a safe investment, return on sales in car retail is often only 1 to 2 %.
Leverage effect: if the return on total capital is above the loan rate, extra debt raises the return on equity. The other way round it lowers it, and risk increases.
Operating result + neutral result = company result. The operating result counts for assessing the business units.
Stock: keep turnover high and storage period short, which saves interest and space. Business units: watch gross profit in % and days in stock per vehicle.
Assessing in the exam: state the value, rate it against a target or comparison (previous year, industry, rule of thumb), name the consequence for the dealership, suggest a suitable measure.

Portfolio: question marks, stars, cash cows, poor dogs (market growth and market share).
Market potential (possible), market volume (actual), market share (own share).
„Kfz-Potenzial“ = inhabitants / 1.000 × cars per 1.000 inhabitants. New car demand per year = „Kfz-Potenzial“ / Ø useful life.
Product life cycle: introduction, growth, maturity (highest sales), saturation, decline. Quarterly planned figure = annual plan × quarter share.
Planned sales = expected market volume × target market share.
Capital requirement = sales × cost price × capital tie-up in days / 360.
Sale and contract
Process: advice, test drive, offer, binding order, check, order confirmation.
The contract only arises with the order confirmation or delivery within the binding period (3 weeks).
Salesperson pay: fixed salary + commission + bonuses. Gross profit commission curbs discounts.
Gross profit = margin − customer discount − extras; commission as a percentage of it.
Invoice and booking

Reversal of burden of proof 12 months. First supplementary performance, then withdrawal or price reduction.
AGB must not unreasonably disadvantage consumers.
Statutory warranty is legal, guarantee voluntary, goodwill without entitlement.
LF 7 · Used cars
Valuation
Purchase price: backwards from the market price minus gross profit, repair, reconditioning, holding costs.
Factors: age, mileage, condition, equipment, colour, previous owners, market situation.
Technical valuation by the workshop, commercial by used car sales (DAT, Schwacke).
Sources: lease returns, auctions, dealers, company cars, online marketplaces.
Taxation and pricing
Margin taxation § 25a: purchase without input VAT; VAT = difference × 19/119; no tax shown.
Standard taxation („MwSt ausweisbar“): purchase with input VAT, 19 % on the net price.
Profit = net margin − repair − reconditioning − holding costs.
Hidden price discount: overpayment on the trade-in, borne by the new car department.

LF 8 · Financial services
Financing
Standard financing: equal instalments down to zero. Balloon/three-way financing: low instalments + final instalment.
Capacity to borrow = legal capacity. Creditworthiness = credit rating (income, SCHUFA, self-disclosure).
Securities: transfer of ownership by way of security (registration certificate II at the bank), salary assignment, guarantee, payment protection insurance.
Effective annual rate = all costs per year. Annuity: instalment equal, interest falls, repayment rises.
Linked transaction: revoking the loan also cancels the purchase.
Captive bank: sales promotion, commission and customer loyalty, low interest and quick approval.
Contractual relationships: purchase contract with the dealership, loan agreement with the bank; the bank pays the loan out to the dealership. Final instalment = expected residual value.
SCHUFA stores accounts, loans, leasing and phone contracts, guarantees. Termination by the bank e.g. for default on 2 instalments, false information or loss of the security.
Leasing
Lessor is owner, lessee is possessor; instalments = expense, not capitalised by the lessee.
Compliant with the tax decree: basic lease term 40–90 % of useful life.
Mileage leasing: extra/fewer kilometres. Residual value leasing: residual value risk with the customer, tender right.
VAT on every instalment. Early end: cancellation, total loss, theft.
Return: report with mileage and damage. Full service: maintenance, tyres, insurance included.
Advantages for the dealership: commission, no default risk, customer loyalty, workshop utilisation, lease returns for the used car business.
Protection
Liability (compulsory), partial cover, comprehensive. Term 1 year, cancel by 30 November.
GAP: difference between settlement value and replacement value. Payment protection insurance: death, incapacity, unemployment.
Security certificate: comprehensive cover payment goes to the bank or lessor.
Statutory warranty is legal, guarantee voluntary, goodwill without entitlement.

Direct: manufacturer sells itself (branch, agency, online). Indirect: via authorised dealers in their own name and for their own account.
Partners: manufacturer/importer, branch, authorised dealer, agent, service partner.

Need → demand with purchasing power → demand on the market.
Free goods cost nothing, economic goods are scarce.
Maximum principle: fixed means, greatest success. Minimum principle: fixed goal, least input.
Sectors: primary production, processing, services.
Simple circular flow: households and companies, flows of goods and money in opposite directions.

Partnerships: OHG, KG, GmbH & Co. KG. Corporations: GmbH (25.000 €), AG (50.000 €).

Commercial register at the local court: A sole traders and partnerships, B corporations. Declaratory or constitutive.
„Istkaufmann“, „Kannkaufmann“, „Formkaufmann“. Firm = name of the merchant in business.

LF 11 · Economic policy
Market and price
Perfect market: homogeneous goods, no preferences, transparency, fast reaction.
The equilibrium price clears the market. Above it excess supply (buyer's market), below it excess demand.
Price functions: balancing, signalling, steering, selection.
Market forms: polypoly, oligopoly, monopoly. Maximum price below, minimum price above equilibrium.
Order and competition
Social market economy: market + social balance + protection of competition.
Cooperation (sub-areas) and concentration (group, merger); horizontal, vertical, diagonal.
Cartels banned in principle; Federal Cartel Office: cartel ban, abuse control, merger control.
Goals, GDP, business cycle
Magic square: price stability, employment, external balance, growth. Hexagon: + distribution, environment.
GDP = consumption + state + investment + net exports; nominal and real; wage share.
Phases: upswing, boom, downturn, trough. Leading, coincident, lagging indicators.
Anticyclical fiscal policy: spend in a downturn, save in a boom.
Money and foreign trade
Inflation reduces purchasing power; measured by the consumer price index (basket of goods).
ECB: price stability; open market, facilities, minimum reserve; expansionary or contractionary.
Balance of payments: current account, capital account, financial account. Net exports = exports − imports.
Globalisation: larger markets, but wage pressure and dependency.
